entries.h: Structure: strong and weak highs and lows
entries.t:
Part 1
Structure: strong and weak highs and lows
Structure gives the direction and the two prices that matter most: where the idea is wrong, and where price is likely to go.

entries.h: Strong and weak points: a downtrend turns up
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram. A downtrend makes three strong highs and three weak lows, each low broken with a BoS. The fourth low is marked strong low, no follow through. Price then breaks the last strong high, marked CHoCH, and climbs through weak highs and strong lows, with demand zones at each strong low and two long position boxes.
ZeusCapital — “Be reactive, not predictive.” A downtrend that turns into an uptrend.
Structure · Bearish to bullish
Strong and weak points: a downtrend turns up
What the diagram shows
The downtrend. Three lows are broken (BoS). Each broken low is a weak low. Each high that produced a break is a strong high, with a supply zone drawn from it.
“No follow through”. The fourth low breaks the one before it, but price does not continue down. It bounces and leaves a small demand zone.
CHoCH. After one more dip into that demand, price closes above the last strong high. The label on the bottom low changes to strong low.
The uptrend. The labels swap. Highs are now weak highs and get broken. Lows are strong lows with demand under them, and they hold.
The two longs. The tall blue boxes are long positions. Each starts where price comes back to a demand zone (mitigation), after small liquidity marked £ has built up and been taken.
How to use the labels
Strong means the point caused a break of structure. Expect it to hold. Your stop goes behind it.
Weak means the point has not broken anything. Expect it to be taken. Your target goes there.
In an uptrend, buy near strong lows and target weak highs. In a downtrend, sell near strong highs and target weak lows.
Why “reactive, not predictive”
Nobody buys the bottom here. At the fourth low there is nothing to act on, only a missing follow through. The first long comes much later, after the CHoCH and two breaks of structure upward. The price is worse and the evidence is better.
Notice also what the old supply zones do after the CHoCH. Price still reacts at two of them, then breaks through. The trend has changed, so they are places to take profit on a long. They are not places to sell.
Rule to carry forward
Label every swing strong or weak before looking for a trade. If you cannot say which low is the strong low, you do not know where the stop goes.

entries.h: The same thing upside down: an uptrend turns down
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram, the mirror of the previous one. An uptrend makes weak highs and strong lows with demand zones. The last high is marked strong high, no follow through. Price breaks the last strong low, marked CHoCH, and falls through weak lows and strong highs, with supply zones and two short position boxes.
ZeusCapital — “Listen to the market.” An uptrend that turns into a downtrend. Dotted blue arrows are marked “mitigation”.
Structure · Bullish to bearish
The same thing upside down: an uptrend turns down
What the diagram shows
The uptrend. Three weak highs are broken. Three strong lows hold, each with demand drawn from it.
“No follow through”. The last high breaks the one before it and stalls. A supply zone forms on the first lower high.
CHoCH. Price closes below the last strong low. The top becomes the strong high.
Mitigation. The dotted blue arrows are price returning to a supply zone. Each return makes a lower strong high, and each is followed by a BoS downward.
The old demand zones. Price reacts at each one on the way down and then breaks it. The line marked £ £ is the liquidity resting under the old strong low.
The two shorts. Both start at a return to supply, after a small cluster of highs and lows (£) or a rising trendline of lows (£) has formed.
What to take from it
The first zone after a CHoCH is not traded in either diagram. Both wait for a break of structure in the new direction and then trade the next return. That costs one leg of the move and removes the trades where the CHoCH was only a deep pullback.
“Strong” is a label, not a guarantee
Both diagrams are drawn after the fact, so every strong point held. On a live chart a strong low is only the low that should hold. When it breaks, that is the CHoCH, and the labels swap.

entries.h: Entry models
entries.t:
Part 2
Entry models
Structure says long or short. The entry model says when the order goes in. The four below use the same zones and differ in how much they wait for.

entries.h: Risk entry and confirmation entry
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram. Price breaks down from a range high to a range low, then climbs back in small steps marked C, B, B, S and B into a supply zone below the range high, marked risk entry. Price drops, breaks an internal low marked C, returns to a smaller zone marked confirmation entry, and falls through the range low.
ZeusCapital — “Type of entries.” Risk entry and confirmation entry on the same short. “These structure breaks are internal structure breaks.”
Entry models · The two basic choices
Risk entry and confirmation entry
What the diagram shows
The swing structure. A BoS down sets a range high and a range low. The trend is down. A supply zone sits under the range high.
The pullback. Price climbs back in small steps. The breaks marked C and B are internal: a small change of character, then small breaks of structure. One is marked S. The slide does not define it. I read it as a high that was matched and not yet broken.
Risk entry. A sell limit at the supply zone, placed in advance. The stop is above the zone.
Confirmation entry. Price rejects the zone and breaks an internal low (C). The drop leaves a smaller zone. The sell goes there on the retest, with the stop above that small zone.
Target. Both aim at the range low.
Internal and swing structure
This is the point of the slide. The pullback looks bullish if you only read the small breaks. It is five internal breaks upward inside one bearish swing. Internal structure tells you when the pullback ends. It does not change the direction, which comes from the range high and range low.
Entry, stop loss, take profit
Entry: Risk: sell limit at the bottom edge of the supply zone. Confirmation: sell limit at the small zone left by the internal break.
Stop loss: Risk: above the supply zone. Confirmation: above the small zone, which on this diagram sits under the high made inside supply.
Take profit: The range low for both. The confirmation entry is lower and its stop is tighter, so the ratio is similar or better.
The trade-off
The risk entry is filled every time price reaches the zone, including the times it goes straight through. The confirmation entry skips those, and also misses the moves that leave without a retest. The site’s entry models page covers the same choice under the names aggressive and confirmation.

entries.h: Aggressive entry: a limit at the order block
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram. Price rises, pulls back to a low that dips under an earlier low, and an order block is drawn there. Price breaks the old high with a BOS to a new high marked target. A falling pullback with a trendline over its highs breaks a low marked with dollar signs and drops into the order block. A position box shows a long from the block to the target.
BSBY — “Aggressive entry.”
Entry model 1 · Aggressive
Aggressive entry: a limit at the order block
What the diagram shows
The order block. It sits at the pullback low. That low dipped under an earlier low first (the arc), so the block comes with a sweep.
BOS. The rise from the block breaks the previous high. That makes the block valid and the low strong.
Liquidity builds. The pullback makes lower highs under a trendline, and a higher low marked $$$.
The fill. Price takes the $$$ low and drops into the block. The order was already there.
Entry, stop loss, take profit
Entry: Buy limit at the top edge of the order block, placed as soon as the BOS confirms.
Stop loss: Below the order block, which is also below the swept low. The yellow box on the slide.
Take profit: The high that made the BOS.
What makes this version acceptable
The block caused a break of structure.
The block’s low swept liquidity when it formed.
Liquidity above the block ($$$) is taken on the way in.
With all three, an order without confirmation is reasonable. With the $$$ low still untouched, the block is more likely the target of a deeper move than the turning point. See inducement.

entries.h: Confirmation entry: wait for the lower timeframe
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram. Two breaks of structure upward. An order block is drawn at the pullback low, with an IDM low above it. Price returns into the block; a circle marked confirmation on LTF shows a small low, a break of a small high and a small shaded entry zone. Price rallies to a new high marked target, pulls back under a trendline of dollar signs into a second order block, and rises again.
BSBY — “SMC.” The circle is marked “Confirmation on LTF”.
Entry model 2 · Confirmation
Confirmation entry: wait for the lower timeframe
What the diagram shows
BOS, then an order block at the low the break came from.
IDM. The first small low above the block. Price breaks it on the way down, so the early buyers are out.
Inside the circle. Price is in the block. On the lower timeframe it makes a low, breaks its last small high, and leaves a small zone (the shaded square). That zone is the entry.
A second chance. After the next BOS, a new order block forms at the base of the leg. A pullback under a $$$ trendline brings price into it, and the trade repeats toward the same high.
Entry, stop loss, take profit
Entry: Buy limit at the small lower-timeframe zone inside the order block.
Stop loss: Below the low made inside the block. If the buffer puts it near the block’s own low, use the block’s low.
Take profit: The high marked target.
Compared with the aggressive entry
Same block, same target. The stop is a fraction of the size, so the same move pays more R. The cost is that you must be watching when price arrives, and some entries will not come back to the small zone.
All eleven case studies on this site are this model.

entries.h: The confirmation entry with every label on it
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram. A BOS upward from an order block at a swept low. The pullback breaks an IDM low, makes lower highs under a trendline of dollar signs, and drops into the order block. Price breaks the last lower high, marked CH, returns to a small order block, and rises to the target at the old high.
FXBY — “SMC entry.”
Entry model 2 · The full checklist
The confirmation entry with every label on it
What the diagram shows
The same model as the last slide, drawn on one timeframe with each step labelled.
Order block at a low that swept an earlier low (the arc), followed by a BOS.
IDM is taken during the pullback.
$$$ builds along the falling highs.
The tap. Price reaches the order block.
CH. Price breaks the last lower high. BSBY and FXBY write CH for change of character.
OB. The small block at the base of that move. Price returns to it and goes to the target.
Entry, stop loss, take profit
Entry: Buy limit at the top edge of the small OB.
Stop loss: Below the low made in the large order block.
Take profit: The old high. The falling highs with $$$ on them are taken on the way.
Rule to carry forward
Five things in order: BOS, inducement taken, zone tapped, change of character, return to the small block. If one is missing, the model is not there yet.

entries.h: When the first reaction low is swept
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram. Two breaks of structure upward from an order block. Price taps the block once and rallies to a new high. A long pullback under a trendline of dollar signs then drops below the low of that first tap, marked with an x and a sweeper icon. Price breaks a lower high marked CH, returns to a zone marked OB/FVG, breaks structure and rises to the target.
BSBY — “SMC.” The sweeper icon marks the liquidity taken under the earlier low.
Entry model 3 · Sweep, then confirm
When the first reaction low is swept
What the diagram shows
The first tap worked. Price took the IDM, reached the order block, and rallied to a new high with a BOS.
The low of that tap is now liquidity. Anyone who bought there has a stop under it.
The second visit goes deeper. After a long pullback with $$$ along its highs, price drops under that low (x). It stays inside the original order block.
CH, then OB/FVG. Price breaks the last lower high and leaves a block or a fair value gap. The entry is there.
BOS upward follows, then the target.
Entry, stop loss, take profit
Entry: Buy limit at the OB/FVG left by the change of character.
Stop loss: Below the sweep low (x).
Take profit: The high marked target.
Why it matters
An aggressive order at the block on the second visit would have filled early and sat in drawdown through the sweep. A stop under the first tap’s low would have been hit. The confirmation entry comes after the sweep, so the sweep becomes the reason for the trade.
A zone that has already been used
A second visit to the same block is weaker than the first. Take it only with a sweep and a change of character, never with a resting limit.

entries.h: Continuation entry: joining a trend that is already running
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram. A downtrend with two breaks of structure. An order block sits at the first high. Lower highs under a curved line form during the decline. After the second break, price rallies through those highs into the order block, drops through a small low, returns to a point marked confirmation entry, and falls through the low marked target.
FXBY — “Continuation entry.” The entry is marked “Confirmation entry”.
Entry model 4 · Continuation
Continuation entry: joining a trend that is already running
What the diagram shows
The trend. Two BOS downward. The order block is at the high the trend started from.
The curve. Three lower highs. Every one has stops above it.
The pullback. Price rallies through all three highs and reaches the order block. Inside the pullback it makes a small high and low, then pushes above that high into the block.
The shift. Price falls through the small low.
The entry. The sell is on the retest after that break.
Target. The last low of the trend, a weak low.
Entry, stop loss, take profit
Entry: Sell limit at the retest after the small low breaks. Use the bottom edge of the zone that the drop left.
Stop loss: Above the high made inside the order block.
Take profit: The low marked target. Price is drawn going through it.
How it differs from a reversal
There is no CHoCH on the larger structure. The trend is intact and you are selling a pullback in it. The sweep that matters is the run through the lower highs, which clears the liquidity above before price turns.

entries.h: Targets and real charts
entries.t:
Part 3
Targets and real charts
Two diagrams on where price goes after the entry, then two candle charts that put the pieces together.

entries.h: Price delivery: from one zone to the next
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram. A downtrend leaves three supply order blocks, one at each lower high. Price reaches a higher-timeframe demand zone, breaks a lower high marked CH, and leaves an order block at the low. From there it rises into the lowest supply block, pulls back to the new order block, rises into the second supply block, with arrows showing a reaction downward at the second and third blocks.
BSBY — “SMC price delivery.”
Targets · Reading the path
Price delivery: from one zone to the next
What the diagram shows
The way down. Each lower high leaves a supply order block. Three are stacked above price.
HTF demand. The last break downward (B) carries price into a higher-timeframe demand zone.
CH. Price breaks the last lower high and leaves an order block at the low.
The way up. Price reaches the nearest supply block and pulls back to the new order block. It then reaches the second supply block. The arrows show a reaction expected at each one.
How to use it
The long is at the order block made by the CH, after the first rise. Stop below the low in HTF demand.
The supply blocks above are the targets, nearest first. They are a ladder for partial profits.
Each block can turn price. The diagram draws arrows down at two of them. Move the stop up only after price has left a new strong low.
Count the room before entering. If the nearest supply block is less than 2R away, the trade does not pay.
Rule to carry forward
A target is the next zone or the next liquidity in the path. Mark every one between entry and the final target before placing the order.

entries.h: The target is the liquidity that built on the way
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram. Price climbs in steps with a curved trendline under its lows marked with dollar signs. A high is swept, marked x, into a higher-timeframe supply zone. Price breaks a low marked CH, returns to an order block at the top, breaks structure and falls to a line marked target at the base of the climb.
BSBY — “SMC [Targets].”
Targets · Trendline liquidity
The target is the liquidity that built on the way
What the diagram shows
The climb. Higher lows along a curved trendline. The lows carry stops, marked $$$.
The sweep. The last push takes the previous high (x) and reaches HTF supply.
CH. Price breaks the last higher low.
OB. The block at the top. Price returns to it, then breaks structure downward.
Target. The low the whole climb started from. Every low on the trendline is taken on the way.
Entry, stop loss, take profit
Entry: Sell limit at the bottom edge of the OB, after the CH.
Stop loss: Above the sweep high, inside HTF supply.
Take profit: The base of the trendline.
A practical note on the target
The base of the trendline is the full target and it is far. Each trendline low before it is a place where price can pause. Taking part of the position at the first one or two is reasonable. The slide shows only the full target.

entries.h: The short from HTF supply on a real chart
entries.t:
Chart: Candlestick chart. Price rallies along a dotted trendline marked liquidity into a higher-timeframe supply zone and peaks. It breaks a low marked CH, then spikes back up through a level marked IDM into the supply zone. A short position box runs from there to a target line at the low the rally started from, which price reaches.
BSBY — “SMC setup.” No pair or timeframe is shown.
On candles · Example 1
The short from HTF supply on a real chart
What the chart shows
Trendline liquidity. A long rally with rising lows.
HTF supply. The rally peaks inside the zone.
CH. Price closes below the last higher low.
IDM. A small high is left just under the peak. One fast candle later takes it and reaches back into supply.
The short. The position box starts at that spike. The stop (yellow) is above the peak.
The path. Price falls, rallies about halfway back without reaching the entry, and then drops to the target.
Entry, stop loss, take profit
Entry: Sell limit in the zone at the top, above the IDM high.
Stop loss: Above the peak, inside HTF supply.
Take profit: The low the rally began from, where the trendline starts.
What the candles add
The diagrams draw clean legs. Here the entry is one fast candle, so a market order would have been late. A resting limit above the IDM high is the practical way to get this fill. The halfway rally in the middle is also normal, and a stop moved to break-even would have survived it on this chart.

entries.h: XAU/USD: sweep of a range into supply
entries.t:
Chart: Candlestick chart of gold. Price rallies leaving a fair value gap, ranges under a higher-timeframe supply zone, and spikes above the range highs, marked x, into the zone. An order block is drawn at the spike. Price drops leaving a fair value gap and breaks a low marked CH, rallies back into the order block, and a short position box runs to a target line at the base of the first rally, which price reaches.
BSBY — “XAU/USD.” No timeframe is shown.
On candles · Example 2
XAU/USD: sweep of a range into supply
What the chart shows
The range. Price stalls under HTF supply and makes several highs at one level.
The sweep (x). One candle spikes above them into the zone. The order block is drawn there.
Displacement. A long candle down leaves a fair value gap and breaks the range low (CH).
The return. Price falls further, then rallies all the way back into the order block.
The short. Entry in the block, stop above it, target at the base of the first rally, where an older FVG was left.
Result. Price reaches the target line.
Entry, stop loss, take profit
Entry: Sell limit at the bottom edge of the OB.
Stop loss: Above the sweep high (the top of the yellow box).
Take profit: The base of the rally. The intermediate low is taken on the way.
What to notice
The retrace was deep and fast. It filled the FVG and reached the block. Waiting for the block gave the fill here. An entry at the FVG would also have filled, with a wider stop. This is the same model as the site’s XAU/USD case study.

entries.h: The four entries side by side
entries.t:
Everything as one
The four entries side by side
Written for longs. Mirror it for shorts.
| | Aggressive (risk) | Confirmation | Sweep, then confirm | Continuation
| Context | BOS up, fresh order block | BOS up, fresh order block | Order block already tapped once | Trend running, no reversal needed
| What you wait for | Nothing after the BOS | Tap of the block, then a change of character | Sweep of the first reaction low, then a change of character | Pullback through the internal highs or lows into the block, then a small shift
| Entry | Limit at the edge of the block | Limit at the small block inside it | Limit at the OB or FVG after the sweep | Limit at the retest after the shift
| Stop | Beyond the block | Beyond the low made in the block | Beyond the sweep low | Beyond the extreme made in the block
| Stop size | Wide | Narrow | Narrow | Narrow
| Target | The high that made the BOS | The same high | The same high | The last weak low or high of the trend
| Main risk | Price goes through the block | No retest, trade missed | The sweep keeps going and becomes a break | The pullback was the start of a reversal
| Screen time | Little | You must watch the tap | You must watch the tap | You must watch the tap
None of the diagrams shows a loss
Every drawing reaches its target. The sources give no win rates, and neither do I. Before trading any of these with money, mark fifty past examples of one model on one pair and record how many reached 2R before the stop. The good and bad BoS page has the site’s one losing example.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
The rules that hold across all four models, written for longs.
Entry
A limit at the near edge of the zone.
Aggressive: the order block that caused the BOS.
Confirmation, sweep and continuation: the small block or FVG left by the change of character.
Only at a zone next to a strong low, in the direction of the swing structure.
Stop loss
Behind the strong point, plus a buffer.
Aggressive: below the order block.
The other three: below the lowest point of the sweep or tap.
If that low breaks, it was not strong and the idea is finished. Do not widen the stop.
Take profit
The nearest weak point or opposing zone.
The weak high that made the last BOS is the standard target.
Opposing order blocks before it are places for partial profit.
Trendline lows or highs are taken on the way to the base of the trendline.
Under 1:2 to the first target, skip the trade.

entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Written for longs. For shorts, mirror it. A “no” at any step ends the process.
Label the swing structure: which highs and lows are strong, which are weak?Uptrend means strong lows and weak highs. If the last strong point has just broken, wait for one break in the new direction.
Mark the zone at the last strong low.The order block the last BOS came from. Note whether it has been tapped before.
Mark the liquidity between price and the zone.IDM lows, equal lows, trendline lows. Expect them to be taken first.
Choose the model before price arrives.Fresh block with a sweep at its low: aggressive is allowed. Tapped block, or any doubt: wait for confirmation.
For confirmation: has price tapped the zone and broken its last lower high?Draw the small block or FVG at the base of that move.
Place the limit, with the stop behind the strong point.Below the block for aggressive. Below the sweep low for the rest.
Mark every zone and liquidity level up to the weak high.The nearest one must be at least 2R away.
Size, place, hold, record.Risk 0.5–1%. Write down which of the four models it was, so the journal can compare them.
Related pages
Entry models compares aggressive and confirmation on one short. Good vs bad BoS covers what makes a low protected. Inducement and types of liquidity cover the marks drawn as £ and $$$. Top-down analysis shows the confirmation entry across four timeframes.

entries.h: Introduction
entries.t:
Concept
Imbalance, supply and demand
Liquidity explains why price moves. Structure gives the direction. Supply and demand zones give the price for the order, and the imbalance is how you tell a real zone from a rectangle drawn on any candle. This page covers how each one forms, which ones to trade, and where the entry, stop and target go.
Imbalance
Demand
Supply
1 · Imbalance
Using an imbalance
2 · Demand
3 · Supply
Which zones to trade
Premium & discount
Everything as one
Entry, SL & TP
Repeatable steps
In the case studies
How to read this page
No screenshots came with this topic, so the diagrams are drawn for this page. They show the definition, not a real trade. Hollow candles close up and solid candles close down. IMB is an imbalance, which other sources call a fair value gap (FVG). An order block (OB) is the single-candle version of a supply or demand zone, and the case studies use the two names for the same job. Definitions differ between teachers. The ones here are the ones this site uses.

entries.h: What an imbalance is
entries.t:
Part 1
What an imbalance is
An imbalance is a stretch of price that was crossed by one candle only. It needs three candles to define.
Candles 1 and 3 do not overlap. The space between the high of candle 1 and the low of candle 3 is the imbalance.
The definition
Bullish. Candle 2 is a strong up candle. The low of candle 3 is above the high of candle 1. The gap between those two prices is the imbalance.
Bearish. Candle 2 is a strong down candle. The high of candle 3 is below the low of candle 1.
If the wicks of candles 1 and 3 overlap, there is no imbalance, however large candle 2 looks.
What it means
Inside the gap, price traded in one direction only. Buyers took every offer and moved on before sellers could trade back. It is a record of urgency. This move, where price leaves quickly and leaves a gap, is called displacement.
Rule to carry forward
Mark an imbalance only when the move that made it also broke structure. Small gaps appear on every low-timeframe chart and most mean nothing.

entries.h: Three uses of an imbalance
entries.t:
Part 1 · In practice
Three uses of an imbalance
1
Proof
A break of structure that leaves an imbalance was made with force. A break that crawls through the level with overlapping candles is weaker. In the case studies the shift almost always comes with an IMB.
2
Magnet
Price often comes back to trade inside the gap before continuing. That is why you can wait for a pullback after a strong move, and why an unfilled gap beyond your target is a reason to hold.
3
Location
The zone the displacement started from sits just beyond the imbalance. The gap leads price back to the zone. An order at the zone is filled after the gap has been filled.
How far it fills
| What price does | What it tells you | What to do
| Never returns | Strong move. The order at the zone is not filled. | Let it go. Do not chase with a market order.
| Fills part of the gap and turns | Strong. Common when the trend is running. | An order at the zone is missed. An order at the middle of the gap is the more aggressive choice, with the stop still beyond the zone.
| Fills the whole gap and reaches the zone | The standard case on this site. | The limit at the edge of the zone fills.
| Closes through the gap and the zone | The move has failed. | The stop is hit. The idea is finished.
Entering at the gap or at the zone
Entering at the imbalance gets more fills and has a wider stop. Entering at the zone has a tighter stop and misses some trades. Pick one and keep to it for a full sample. Mixing them trade by trade makes the journal useless.

entries.h: Demand: where buying started
entries.t:
Part 2
Demand: where buying started
A demand zone is the last place sellers were in control before buyers moved price far enough to break structure.
The last down candle before the move that broke structure. The zone runs from its low to its open and is extended to the right.
How to draw it
Find the break. A close above a previous high, made by strong candles that leave an imbalance.
Walk back to the start of that move. The last down candle before it is the zone.
Mark two prices. The low of that candle, including the wick, is the far edge. The open of that candle is the near edge. If the candle is very small, use its high as the near edge.
If price paused for a few small candles before leaving, draw the zone around the whole pause.
Extend it to the right until price comes back.
Why price reacts there
The usual explanation is that large buyers could not fill their whole order before price left, and buy again when it returns. Nobody can verify that from a chart. What you can verify is the behaviour: price left this level fast and broke structure. Treat the zone as a level to test, not as a promise.
Fresh and used
Fresh: price has not returned since the zone formed. This is the one to trade.
Mitigated: price has returned once and reacted. A second visit is weaker. Trade it only with a sweep and a shift on the lower timeframe. See sweep, then confirm.
Broken: a candle has closed below the far edge. Delete it.

entries.h: Supply: where selling started
entries.t:
Part 3
Supply: where selling started
The mirror image. A supply zone is the last up candle before a move that broke structure downward.
The last up candle before the move that broke structure downward. The zone runs from its high to its open.
How to draw it
Find the break. A close below a previous low, with an imbalance.
Walk back to the start of that move. The last up candle before it is the zone.
Mark two prices. The high of that candle, including the wick, is the far edge. The open is the near edge.
The edges for a short
For supply, the near edge is the bottom of the zone. That is where the sell limit goes. The stop goes above the top. It is easy to get this backwards when you have been looking at longs. The XAU/USD and GBP/USD shorts both sell the bottom edge.
Spread on shorts
Charts show the bid price. A short is closed at the ask, which is higher by the spread. Add the spread to the stop above a supply zone, or a wick that never shows on the chart can close the trade.

entries.h: Which zones are worth trading
entries.t:
Selection
Which zones are worth trading
Any chart has dozens of last-down candles. Six questions cut them down. The first three are required.
| Question | Why it matters | If the answer is no
| 1. Did the move from the zone break structure? | Without a break, nothing shows the zone had any effect. | Not a zone. Do not draw it.
| 2. Did it leave an imbalance? | Shows price left with force. | Skip it.
| 3. Is it fresh? | A zone that has been tested has already done its work. | Only with lower-timeframe confirmation.
| 4. Did the zone’s extreme sweep liquidity? | The stops under an old low were taken when the zone formed, so there is less reason for price to dig under it again. | Expect a deeper move. Look for the zone below that did sweep.
| 5. Is it on the right side of the range? | Demand in discount, supply in premium. See the next section. | Poor reward-to-risk. Usually skip.
| 6. Does it agree with the higher timeframe? | A 15m demand zone inside a 4H demand zone has two reasons to hold. | Counter-trend. Smaller target or skip.
Liquidity in front of the zone
If small equal lows sit just above a demand zone, the zone is better, because price has a reason to come down to it. If a clean zone sits above an untouched origin zone with liquidity under it, the upper zone is likely the trap. That is covered in inducement.

entries.h: Premium and discount
entries.t:
Location
Premium and discount
Split the current swing in half. Buy in the lower half and sell in the upper half.
Two demand zones in the same leg. Only the one below the midpoint leaves room to the high.
How to use it
Take the swing from the last strong low to the high it made (for longs).
Mark 50%. Below it is discount, above it is premium.
Buy only from demand in discount. A zone in premium is close to the high, so the target is near and the stop is the same size. The numbers do not work.
For shorts, sell only from supply in premium.
This is an arithmetic rule more than a market theory. It makes sure the distance to the target is larger than the distance to the stop before you look at anything else.

entries.h: Liquidity, structure, imbalance and zone in one trade
entries.t:
Everything as one
Liquidity, structure, imbalance and zone in one trade
The same order of events as every case study on this site.
Equal lows are swept. One leg breaks structure and leaves an imbalance. The demand zone is the base of that leg. Price returns through the gap to the zone.
1
Sweep
Price takes the equal lows (X). The low of the sweep becomes the far edge of the zone.
2
Displacement
One leg closes above the last lower high (MSS) and leaves an imbalance. Now the zone is valid.
3
Return
Price fills the imbalance and reaches the near edge of the demand zone. The limit fills. The target is the weak high.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
For a long from demand. Reverse every edge for a short from supply.
Entry
Buy limit at the near (top) edge of the demand zone.
Place it when the candle that broke structure has closed.
In six of the eleven case studies price only touched the edge. An order deeper in the zone would have been missed.
For supply: sell limit at the bottom edge.
Stop loss
Below the far edge of the zone, plus a buffer.
The far edge is the wick low. If that low was a sweep, the stop is under the sweep.
A close below the zone means it has failed. Do not move the stop down.
For supply: above the wick high, plus spread.
Take profit
The first opposing zone or untouched liquidity.
The weak high that the displacement made is the standard target.
If a fresh supply zone sits before it, close there, or close part.
Set the order a little before the level.
Less than 1:2, skip the trade.

entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Written for longs. For shorts, mirror it. A “no” at any step ends the process.
Is the higher timeframe bullish, and is price in the discount half of its swing?If price is in premium, wait for it to come down.
Has a move just closed above a previous high?That is the break. No break, no zone.
Did that move leave an imbalance?Check that the wicks of candles 1 and 3 do not overlap.
Mark the last down candle before the move.Low to open. Extend it right.
Is the zone fresh, and did its low sweep an earlier low?Fresh is required. The sweep makes it the better zone.
Is there liquidity between price and the zone?Good. Expect it to be taken before the fill.
Buy limit at the top edge, stop under the wick low.Or wait for a lower-timeframe shift inside the zone and use the smaller zone it leaves.
Is the first opposing zone or high at least 2R away?If not, skip it.
Size, place, hold, record.Risk 0.5–1%. Record whether price touched the edge, went deep, or never came back.

entries.h: Introduction
entries.t:
Concept
Top-down analysis: 4H, 1H, 30m, 5m
One long, read from the largest chart to the smallest. Each timeframe answers one question and hands the next one a smaller area to look at. The 4H gives the trend. The 1H says the pullback may be ending. The 30m gives the zone. The 5m gives the entry. By the time an order is placed, four charts agree.
Drawn as a long
No pair named
Target reached · ≈ 1:2.5
1 · 4H trend
2 · 1H shift
3 · 30m zone
4 · 5m confirmation
5 · The order
6 · Result
Everything as one
30m or 5m entry?
Entry, SL & TP
Repeatable steps
How to read this page
X marks a liquidity sweep. SSL and BSL are sell-side and buy-side liquidity. EQH is equal highs. $$ marks resting liquidity. The slide captions are quoted under each chart. The slides name no pair and show no price or time, so anything beyond the captions is my reading. Reward-to-risk is measured from the position box.

entries.h: 4H: bullish, and pulling back
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour chart. Price rises through three breaks of structure to a peak, then declines steadily and drops back to about the level of the last break.
Slide 1 — “4h Timeframe. Price is clearly bullish and currently in a pullback phase.” (The slide prints “fullback”.)
4H · Direction
4H: bullish, and pulling back
What the slide shows
Three breaks of structure upward. Higher highs and higher lows.
A peak, then a slow decline. It ends with one sharp drop.
Price now. Back near the level of the last BoS, well above the lows of the trend.
The question this chart answers
Which side? Long. The trend is up and no 4H low has been broken. The decline is a pullback, which means price is getting cheaper inside an uptrend.
The 4H does not say where the pullback ends. It could stop here or go much deeper.
Rule to carry forward
Start on the 4H. Write down one word, long or short, from the last breaks of structure. If you cannot, there is no trade today on this pair.

entries.h: 1H: the pullback shifts back up
entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour chart. Price declines in steps, breaks below an earlier low (BoS), makes a new low labelled SSL, then one large bullish candle closes above the last lower high (MSS). A BSL line marks the high far above. Price is pulling back after the shift.
Slide 2 — “1h Timeframe. On the 1h timeframe, we see a Market Structure Shift (MSS) indicating that the pullback might end and price is ready for continuation.”
1H · Timing
1H: the pullback shifts back up
What the slide shows
The pullback in detail. Lower highs and lower lows on the 1H.
BoS down. Price breaks below the low at the left of the chart. The stops under that low are taken.
A new low (SSL). The lowest point of the pullback.
MSS. One large bullish candle closes above the last lower high.
BSL. A line at the high the 1H decline began from.
The question this chart answers
Is the pullback finished? Possibly. The slide says “might”. The 1H was making lower highs. It has now closed above one, straight after taking an old low. That is a sweep followed by a shift, on the timeframe one below the trend.
Two levels are now fixed. The SSL low is where the idea is wrong. The BSL high is where price is likely headed if it is right.
Rule to carry forward
On the 1H, wait for the pullback to take a low and then close above its last lower high. Before that, the 4H trend is not a reason to buy.

entries.h: 30m: the order block the shift came from
entries.t:
Chart: 30-minute chart. After the decline and the low labelled SSL, a large bullish candle breaks the prior high (MSS). A 30-minute order block is drawn at its base. A short line marked with dollar signs sits just above the order block, and price is drifting down toward it.
Slide 3 — “30m Timeframe. We can actually take a trade from this 30m OB, but for higher probability, we drop down to a lower timeframe for confirmation.”
30m · Location
30m: the order block the shift came from
What is marked
MSS. The same shift as on the 1H, seen closer.
30m OB. A box at the base of the candle that made it.
SSL. The pullback low, under the order block.
$$. A short line just above the order block, at the low price is making on its way back down.
The question this chart answers
Where do I look for the entry? At the 30m order block. It is the origin of the move that shifted structure, and the low beneath it has already swept an older low.
The $$ line is a warning. A small low is forming just above the block. Buyers who enter there will have stops under it, between price and the zone. Expect that low to be taken.
The caption gives a choice here. See 30m or 5m entry? below.

entries.h: 5m: sweep and shift at the 30m order block
entries.t:
Chart: 5-minute chart. Price spikes up from the 30-minute order block, then drifts down under a descending dotted line marked with dollar signs. An internal low is swept (X) by a candle that reaches the top of the 30-minute order block. Price then closes above a prior high (MSS), leaving an imbalance and a narrow 5-minute order block. Two highs at the same level are marked EQH.
Slide 4 — “5m Timeframe. On the 5m timeframe, price swept the internal low, filled the imbalance, and tapped into the 30m OB. An MSS formed, leaving a new IMB and 5m OB.”
5m · Confirmation
5m: sweep and shift at the 30m order block
What the slide shows
The drift back down. Lower highs line up under a dotted line with $$$. That is trendline liquidity above price.
The sweep (X). One candle takes the internal low and reaches the top of the 30m OB.
MSS. The next push closes above the last 5m high.
IMB and 5m OB. The push leaves an imbalance. A narrow order block is drawn at its base, just above the 30m OB.
EQH. After the shift, price makes two highs at the same level and turns down.
The question this chart answers
Is the zone being defended right now? Yes. The caption lists four things in order: internal low swept, imbalance filled, 30m OB tapped, MSS. That is the full sequence again, on the smallest chart, inside the zone the larger charts pointed to.
The equal highs are liquidity. They are close, clean and untouched, so they become the target.

entries.h: Entry, stop and target from the caption
entries.t:
Chart: 5-minute chart with the long planned. The position box has its entry at the top of the 5-minute order block, its stop just under the SSL line at the sweep low, and its target at the EQH line.
Slide 5 — “5m Timeframe. We placed our entry at the 5m OB, with SL below the internal low and TP target at the EQH.”
5m · The order
Entry, stop and target from the caption
What is marked
Entry: the top edge of the 5m OB.
Stop: under the low of the sweep, labelled SSL on this slide. It sits at the top of the 30m OB.
Target: the equal highs.
Reading the box
The target is about 2.5 times the stop. It is the nearest liquidity above, not the 1H BSL, which is much further away. The post takes the close, likely target and leaves the far one.
The stop is under the 5m sweep low. It is not under the 30m OB. If price goes deeper into the 30m block, this trade is stopped even though the 30m idea is still alive.

entries.h: Result: an edge fill, one deep wick, then the equal highs
entries.t:
Chart: 5-minute result. Price drifts down from the equal highs to the top of the 5-minute order block and fills the long. One long wick goes through the order block without reaching the stop. Price then rallies to the equal highs and wicks above them.
Slide 6 — “5m Timeframe. Result.”
Result
Result: an edge fill, one deep wick, then the equal highs
What happened
A slow drift down. Price slid from the equal highs back toward the 5m OB.
The fill. Several candles sat on the top edge of the block.
One deep wick. A single wick went through nearly the whole 5m OB. It stopped above the stop.
The rally. A few large candles carried price to the equal highs, and a wick went through them.
What to take from it
The block was narrow and the wick went through all of it. A stop under the block, not under the sweep low, would have been hit.
The target was liquidity that formed after the shift. Price took it and the chart ends there.

entries.h: Four charts, four questions
entries.t:
Everything as one
Four charts, four questions
Chart: Cover slide: How To Find A High Probability Setup, step-by-step top-down analysis, showing the finished 5-minute long.
Cover — “How To Find A High Probability Setup (Step-by-Step Top-Down Analysis).”
| Timeframe | Question | Answer on this chart | What it hands down
| 4H | Which side? | Long. Uptrend, in a pullback | A direction
| 1H | Is the pullback ending? | An old low taken, then an MSS up | The low that must hold (SSL) and the high to aim for (BSL)
| 30m | Where is the zone? | The order block at the base of the shift | An area to watch
| 5m | Is it being defended now? | Internal low swept at the block, then an MSS with an imbalance | Entry, stop and a near target
Each chart looks only inside what the one above it marked. The 5m is never read on its own. A 5m sweep and shift somewhere else on the chart would mean nothing.
1 · 4H
Bullish, pulling back. Longs only.
2 · 1H
The pullback takes an old low, then closes above its last lower high.
3 · 30m
The order block at the base of that shift. A small low with $$ forms above it.
4 · 5m
That low is swept into the block. The 5m shifts up and leaves a narrow order block and equal highs.
5 · ORDER
Buy limit at the 5m block, stop under the sweep low, target the equal highs. About 2.5R.
THE LOGIC IN ONE SENTENCE
Take direction from the 4H, timing from the 1H, the zone from the 30m and the entry from the 5m, and only when all four agree.

entries.h: Enter at the 30m order block, or wait for the 5m?
entries.t:
The choice in the caption
Enter at the 30m order block, or wait for the 5m?
The post says: “We can actually take a trade from this 30m OB, but for higher probability, we drop down to a lower timeframe for confirmation.” Both are valid. They are the two entry models applied one level down.
| | Limit at the 30m OB | Wait for the 5m sweep and shift
| Entry | Top edge of the 30m OB, placed in advance | Top edge of the 5m OB, placed after the 5m MSS
| Stop | Under the 30m OB, or under the SSL low | Under the 5m sweep low
| Stop size | Wide | Narrow
| Evidence before entry | None on the lower timeframe | A sweep and a shift at the zone
| Screen time | Little. Set the order and leave | You have to be watching the 5m when price arrives
| Main risk | Price goes through the zone | Price leaves without a clean 5m pattern and you miss it, or a small wick takes the tight stop
| On this chart | Price reached the top of the block, so it would have filled, and the SSL low held | Filled and reached the target
“High probability” is a claim, not a measurement
More agreement between timeframes should filter out weaker trades. It also means fewer trades and tighter stops, and tighter stops are hit by noise more often. The post gives no numbers. One example cannot show whether the 5m confirmation raises the win rate enough to pay for the trades it misses. Backtest both versions on the same setups and compare.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
For the 5m version, as drawn on slide 5.
Entry
Buy limit at the top edge of the 5m OB.
The block is the base of the 5m MSS move, under its imbalance, just above the 30m OB.
Place the order when the 5m MSS candle closes.
On a 5m entry the spread is a real share of the stop. Allow for it.
Stop loss
Below the 5m sweep low, plus a buffer.
The caption calls it “below the internal low”. On slide 5 the box ends just under the SSL line.
Not just under the 5m OB. The result shows a wick through the whole block.
The wider choice is under the 1H SSL low. Use it with the 30m entry, not with this one.
Take profit
The equal highs (EQH). About 2.5R.
The nearest clean liquidity above the entry.
Set the order a little before the level.
The 1H BSL is the further target. The post does not use it. If you want to hold a part for it, close most at the EQH first.

entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Written for longs. For shorts, mirror it. A “no” at any step ends the process.
4H: is structure breaking upward, and is price pulling back?Write “long”. If the 4H is unclear, stop.
1H: has the pullback taken a low and then closed above its last lower high?Mark the pullback low (SSL) and the high above (BSL).
30m: draw the order block at the base of that shift.Set an alert at its top edge. Mark any small low forming above it as liquidity.
Decide now: 30m entry or 5m confirmation.Do not decide when price arrives.
5m: when price reaches the block, is an internal low swept?The sweep should reach the 30m OB.
5m: does a candle close above the last 5m high with an imbalance?Draw the 5m OB at the base of that move.
Buy limit at the 5m OB, stop under the sweep low.Target the nearest clean highs above.
Does it pay at least 1:2?If not, skip it.
Size, place, hold, record.Risk 0.5–1%. Screenshot all four timeframes.
Other ladders on this site
The timeframes can change as long as the jobs stay the same. GBP/JPY used 1H, 15m and 5m. USD/JPY used 1H, 30m and 15m. The first USD/JPY case used 4H, 30m and 15m. The playbook routine is built on the same order.

entries.p: AUD/USD Short From the 1H Order Block
entries.h: 1H: an old high is swept, structure shifts down
entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour AUD/USD chart. Price falls from a high at the left, recovers over a long period, and pushes above that old high, marked X. It then turns down and breaks below a prior low (MSS). A 1-hour order block is drawn at the last candles before the drop, and price is climbing back toward it.
Slide 1 — “1h Timeframe.”
Step 1 · Higher-timeframe bias and zone
1H: an old high is swept, structure shifts down
What happened
An old high at the left. Price fell a long way from it, then spent the rest of the chart climbing back.
The sweep (X). The rally pushed above that old high. It stayed above for a short while and made no further progress.
MSS down. Price rolled over and closed below the last higher low of the rally.
The 1H order block. A box at the last candles before the drop that made the shift.
The return. Price bounces and is heading back up toward the block as the chart ends.
Why this matters
The rally looked like a recovery. It ended by taking the stops above the old high and then breaking its own structure. That is a sweep followed by a shift on the 1H, so the bias is short. The order block is where to look for the entry.
Rule to carry forward
When the 1H takes an old high and then closes below its last higher low, mark the order block the drop came from. Wait for price to return to it and change to the 15m.

entries.p: AUD/USD Short From the 1H Order Block
entries.h: 15m: sweep and shift inside the 1H order block
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute AUD/USD chart with the short planned. Price rallies into the 1-hour order block, sweeps a high (X) and tops. It declines and breaks a low (MSS), spikes back up to a lower high, then drops sharply, leaving a 15-minute order block and an imbalance, and breaks structure (BoS). A small high is marked IDM. The position box has its entry at the bottom of the 15-minute order block, its stop above the lower high and its target at the SSL line at the far-left low.
Slide 2 — “15m Timeframe.” The large box at the top left is the 1H OB.
Step 2 · Confirmation and plan
15m: sweep and shift inside the 1H order block
What happened
The rally into the 1H OB. From the low at the far left, price climbs into the block.
A sweep inside it (X). A 15m high is taken and price tops just above. The line across the chart marks that top.
MSS. Price drifts down and closes below a 15m low.
A spike to a lower high. Price jumps back into the lower part of the 1H OB. It stops short of the top.
The drop. A sharp fall from that lower high leaves an imbalance (IMB). The 15 OB is drawn at its origin.
BoS. After a pause, price breaks the low under the MSS and keeps falling.
IDM. The pause left a small high between price and the 15m OB.
The position box
Entry: the bottom edge of the 15m OB.
Stop: above the lower high the drop came from. That is above the 15m OB and below the top of the rally.
Target: the SSL line, drawn from the low at the far left where the rally began. About 2.5 times the stop.
Price had already fallen a long way
When this plan was drawn, price had dropped most of the distance to the target and bounced. The order was still left in place. The target had not been touched and the IDM high and imbalance were still open above. Many traders would have cancelled here. See the note under “When to skip”.

entries.p: AUD/USD Short From the 1H Order Block
entries.h: Result: inducement taken, edge fill, straight to the low
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute AUD/USD result. Price rallies back through the IDM high and the imbalance, a wick reaches the bottom edge of the 15-minute order block, and price then falls in an almost straight line through the SSL line.
Slide 3 — “Result.”
Step 3 · Result
Result: inducement taken, edge fill, straight to the low
What happened
The pullback. Price climbed back from the lows in a few large candles.
IDM taken. It went through the small high from the pause. Anyone who sold there with a stop above it was taken out.
IMB filled, OB touched. One wick reached just into the bottom edge of the 15m OB. The sell limit filled.
The drop. Price fell almost without a pause to the SSL line and well through it.
What to take from it
The fill was a wick at the edge. An order placed deeper in the block would not have filled.
The stop was never approached.
The inducement high was the bait. The fill came one step above it.

entries.p: AUD/USD Short From the 1H Order Block
entries.h: The whole trade on one page
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole trade on one page
Chart: Cover slide: AUDUSD, showing the finished 15-minute short from the order block to the SSL line.
Cover — “AUDUSD.” The finished trade.
1 · BIAS
The 1H takes an old high and shifts structure down. Short bias.
2 · LOCATION
The 1H order block at the origin of that shift. Price climbs back into it.
3 · SWEEP AND SHIFT
Inside the block the 15m sweeps a high, breaks a low, makes a lower high and drops with an imbalance.
4 · ZONE
The 15m order block at the origin of the drop. An inducement high forms under it.
5 · ENTRY AND TARGET
Price takes the inducement, touches the block and fills the sell limit. It falls through the low the rally began from. About 2.5R.
THE LOGIC IN ONE SENTENCE
After a 1H sweep and shift down, let price return to the 1H order block, wait for the 15m to sweep and shift there, and sell the 15m order block toward the low.
This is the full sequence mirrored for a short and run on two timeframes. It is also the short-side twin of the second USD/JPY case.

entries.p: AUD/USD Short From the 1H Order Block
entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Sell limit at the bottom edge of the 15m OB.
The block is at the origin of the sharp drop, above the imbalance.
Only a wick reached it. The edge is the price that filled.
Do not sell the IDM high below it. That high was taken first.
Sells fill on the bid, so no spread needs adding to the limit price.
Stop loss
Above the swing high over the 15m OB, plus spread and a buffer.
The grey box ends just above the lower high the drop came from.
If price goes back above that high, the 15m shift has failed.
Buy stops trigger on the ask. Add the spread to the stop price.
The wider alternative is above the top of the rally, the line across the chart. It lowers the ratio.
Take profit
The SSL line: the low the rally started from. About 2.5R.
It is the low left by the 1H shift, where the climb back to the order block began.
Price went well through it. The plan still exits at the line.
Set the order a few pips above the level.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
While waiting: cancel if price touches the SSL line before filling you, or if a 15m candle closes above the 15m OB.
Once filled: leave the stop alone until price breaks the low made before the pullback.
News: check the calendar for AUD and USD releases before leaving an order or a position open.
Position size
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the lot size.
Lots = money at risk ÷ (stop in pips × pip value per lot)
On AUD/USD one standard lot moves $10 per pip.
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. Stop of 12 pips gives 100 ÷ (12 × 10) ≈ 0.83 lots. At 1:2.5 the target pays about $250. The 12 pips is an illustration. The slides show no prices.

When this setup should be skipped

entries.p: AUD/USD Waiting for the Real Zone
entries.h: H4: bullish, back at demand, not an entry yet
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour AUD/USD chart. Price rallies from a swept low, makes a high, then pulls back to a demand zone whose top sits at the 0.5 level. A wick runs through the bottom of the zone (X) and price closes back above.
Slide 1 — H4 chart. “H4 bias is bullish. Price returns to demand. Not an entry yet.”
Step 1 · Bias and location
H4: bullish, back at demand, not an entry yet
What happened
The rally began with a sweep. The small X at the bottom left marks a low that was run before price turned up.
Price made a strong leg higher. A run of bullish candles to a swing high. The line drawn across the top marks that high. It becomes the target.
Demand sits at the midpoint. The red 0.5 line is the halfway point of the leg. The demand zone's top edge is on it, so the whole zone is in discount.
Price came back and wicked through the zone (X). One candle's wick ran the full depth of the demand zone and slightly below its low, then closed back above. The next candle is bullish.
Why this is “not an entry yet”
Everything on this chart is favourable: bullish structure, a pullback into discount, a demand zone, and a sweep of the zone's own low. But an H4 candle covers four hours. This slide tells you where to look and which way. It cannot tell you where buyers actually stepped in, or where a stop of sensible size would go.
Rule to carry forward
H4 gives bias and location only. When price reaches H4 demand in discount, move to the M15 and start again from the beginning: what was swept, has structure shifted, where is the zone.

entries.p: AUD/USD Waiting for the Real Zone
entries.h: M15: price takes the low, then structure shifts
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute AUD/USD chart. Price drops through a range low (X) into the H4 demand zone, reverses sharply, sweeps a small low (X), then closes above the previous high (MSS). A 15-minute demand zone and an inducement low (IDM) are marked.
Slide 2 — M15 chart. “Price takes the low, then structure shifts. Now there is a reason to look for an entry.”
Step 2 · Confirmation
M15: price takes the low, then structure shifts
What happened
A range formed above the H4 zone. Hours of sideways movement left a clear low. The long X line runs along it.
The range low was swept into H4 demand. One hard drop took out the low, went the full depth of the large olive box and slightly beneath it. This is the H4 wick from slide 1, seen up close.
Price reversed just as hard. A V-shaped recovery back into the range.
A second, smaller sweep (short X). Price dipped once more and ran a minor low left by the recovery, then turned.
MSS. The next leg closed above the high of the recovery. It left an imbalance (IMB).
M15 demand is drawn at the origin. The smaller box labelled Demand covers the base of that leg, from under the imbalance down to the low of the small sweep.
IDM. The first small pullback low after the shift is marked as inducement.
Why this matters
This is the sequence from the other case studies: liquidity taken inside a higher-timeframe zone, then a shift with displacement. The M15 demand is the refined zone inside the H4 one. From here there is a reason to plan a long.
The IDM label is the new idea. That first pullback low is the obvious place for early buyers to put their stops. Until it has been taken, the pullback has not really started.
Rule to carry forward
After the MSS, mark two things: the demand zone at the origin of the shift, and the first pullback low above it. The zone is where you buy. The low is liquidity that price will probably take on the way there.

entries.p: AUD/USD Waiting for the Real Zone
entries.h: A small structure forms. It looks like the entry.
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute AUD/USD chart with the long planned. Price ranges for hours above the demand zone, fails at the range high, drops through the inducement low and bounces, leaving a low marked with dollar signs just above the demand zone. The entry is at the top of the demand zone.
Slide 3 — M15 chart with the order planned. “A small structure forms. It looks like the entry. But there is liquidity still waiting below.”
Step 3 · The entries that were early
A small structure forms. It looks like the entry.
What happened
Price ranged for about ten hours. After the shift it went sideways near the highs. The dotted line marks the top of that range.
The range high held. A late push came close to the earlier high and failed.
Price dropped through the inducement. A sharp fall took out the IDM low and the lows of the range.
It bounced before reaching demand. A strong bullish candle followed straight away. This is the “small structure”: inducement taken, a sharp rejection, a higher-timeframe bullish bias. It looks like the entry.
The bounce left a low ($$$). That low sits just above the M15 demand zone. Anyone who bought the bounce has a stop under it.
Why it was not the entry
Price turned in empty space. There is no zone where it bounced. The M15 demand is still beneath it and still untouched.
The bounce created fresh liquidity directly on top of that zone.
The move down had taken the inducement and had not yet reached the place the shift came from.
The slide shows the plan that respects this: entry at the top edge of the M15 demand, stop below the zone, target at the H4 high.
Rule to carry forward
A reaction is only an entry if it happens at your zone. If price bounces above an untouched zone, the bounce has made a new low for price to come back and take. Keep the order at the zone.
Two early entries on this chart
The first was buying H4 demand on touch in slide 1, which was followed by the hard drop through the zone. The second was buying this bounce. Both were in the right direction. Both were stopped or deep in drawdown before the move began.

entries.p: AUD/USD Waiting for the Real Zone
entries.h: Only then does price reach the real zone
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute AUD/USD chart after the trade. Price falls through the dollar-sign low into the demand zone, reverses, ranges, pulls back once, then rallies to the high at the top of the chart.
Slide 4 — result. “Only then does price reach the real zone. This is where the move starts.”
Step 4 · Fill, management and outcome
Only then does price reach the real zone
What happened
The $$$ low was taken. Shortly after midnight on the chart, price fell through it. Buyers of the bounce were stopped out.
Price entered the M15 demand and went deep. The limit order at the top edge filled, and price carried on more than halfway through the zone.
The bottom of the zone held. A few candles based inside it, then price left sharply.
The move was not a straight line. Price rallied, ranged for a couple of hours, and gave back a large part of the first leg before continuing.
Target reached. Price climbed to the H4 high and wicked through it.
What to take from it
The wait was about thirteen hours from the shift to the fill. The trade itself took roughly nine more.
The fill was deep. As with Bitcoin, a stop inside the zone would have been hit. It has to go under the whole zone.
Three layers of liquidity were cleared before the entry: the inducement low, the range lows, and the $$$ low. Each one was a group of early buyers.
The mid-trade pullback was a test of management. Price retraced deeply on the way to target. A stop moved to breakeven too soon is at risk on a pullback like that.
Rule to carry forward
Before acting, list what has to happen first. Here it was: inducement taken, liquidity above the zone taken, price inside the zone. Two of three is not enough.

A schematic of the M15 sequence, not a copy of the chart. The H4 is already bullish and price is arriving at H4 demand.
1 · SWEEP INTO H4 DEMAND
Price takes the range low (X) and drives through the H4 demand zone, then reverses hard. Buying the H4 zone on touch was the first early entry.
2 · SHIFT
After a second small sweep, the M15 closes above the recovery high. The imbalance and the M15 demand mark where the move began.
3 · INDUCEMENT AND A FALSE START
Price ranges, drops through the IDM low and bounces above the zone. Buying that bounce was the second early entry. It leaves the $$$ low.
4 · THE REAL ZONE
Price takes the $$$ low and trades deep into the M15 demand. The limit order fills about thirteen hours after the shift.
5 · TARGET
Price rallies, pulls back once, and reaches the H4 swing high. About 3.2R.
THE LOGIC IN ONE SENTENCE
With H4 bias, buy the M15 demand at the origin of the shift, and only after the inducement and the lows above the zone have been taken.

entries.p: AUD/USD Waiting for the Real Zone
entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Buy limit at the top edge of the M15 demand zone.
The zone is the base of the leg that made the MSS, directly under the imbalance.
Place it after the shift and leave it through the range and the bounce.
Price went more than halfway through the zone. The top-edge entry filled early and sat in drawdown before turning.
Buys fill on the ask. Add the spread to the limit price.
Stop loss
Below the bottom of the M15 demand zone, plus a buffer.
The bottom of the zone is the low of the small sweep that launched the MSS. If it breaks, the shift is void.
On the chart the grey box ends a fraction below the zone. That gap is the buffer.
It is not under the H4 zone's low. That would be safer and would roughly double the risk on this chart.
Do not tighten it into the zone. This trade needed most of that room.
Take profit
The H4 swing high. About 3.2R.
It is the high marked on the H4 slide: the top of the leg price is pulling back from.
With H4 bullish, a return to that high is the minimum expectation for the next leg.
The top of the M15 range lies on the way and is taken first.
Price wicked through the level here. Set the order a few pips before it regardless.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
While waiting: cancel if an M15 candle closes below the demand zone, or if price reaches the H4 high without filling you.
Once filled: expect drawdown inside the zone. Leave the stop where it is.
On the way up: trail only behind a confirmed M15 higher low after a new high. This trade pulled back deeply mid-way, and a breakeven stop moved after the first rally may or may not have survived it.
Position size
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the lot size.
Lots = money at risk ÷ (stop in pips × pip value per lot)
On AUD/USD one standard lot moves $10 per pip, because the pair is quoted in US dollars.
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. Stop of 20 pips gives 100 ÷ (20 × 10) = 0.50 lots. At 1:3.2 the target pays about $320.

entries.p: BTC/USD What Happens After the Sweep
entries.h: After the sweep, the move looks obvious
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute Bitcoin chart. Price falls through a series of lows, a wick marks the final low (X), then price closes above the bounce high (MSS), rallies, spikes down to a low marked with dollar signs, and breaks to a new high (BoS). An order block sits above the protected low.
Slide 1 — 15m chart. “What Happens After the Sweep.”
Step 1 · Sweep, shift and the temptation
After the sweep, the move looks obvious
What happened
Price sold off through a staircase of lows. The dashed lines on the left mark earlier lows, each one broken in turn. The olive box is not labelled; it looks like an earlier demand zone that price drove straight through.
The final low was a sweep (X). After the large bearish candle, price bounced, then a wick reached slightly lower and was rejected. That wick's low becomes the protected low.
MSS. One large bullish candle closed above the high of the bounce. The 15m downtrend is over. The candle left an imbalance (IMB) at its base.
The order block is drawn wide. The grey OB box runs from just under the imbalance all the way down to the protected low. It covers the whole base that the shift launched from.
A violent pullback stopped short ($$). After a first rally, one big bearish candle fell most of the way back and turned just above the order block. Its low is marked as liquidity.
BoS. The next candles reversed that entire drop and broke to a new high.
Why this is the dangerous moment
At the end of this slide everything agrees: sweep, shift, break of structure, strong candles. The order block was never touched, so a trader with a limit order there has no position, and price is far above. This is where the post says “you want to enter now”.
Two things on the chart argue for waiting. The order block is still fresh. And there is now a clean low marked $$ sitting directly above it, with the stops of everyone who bought that dip resting underneath.
Rule to carry forward
A pullback that turns just short of your order block has not cancelled the setup. It has added liquidity in front of it. Leave the order where it is.
Common mistake
Buying the breakout at the highs with a stop under the $$ low. That stop sits exactly where price is most likely to go next.

entries.p: BTC/USD What Happens After the Sweep
entries.h: Wait for price to return to the zone
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute Bitcoin chart with the long planned. Price has made a new high marked BSL and is ranging. The entry is at the top of the order block, the stop is below the protected low and the target is the BSL high.
Slide 2 — 15m chart with the order planned. “Wait for Price to Return to the Zone.”
Step 2 · The plan
Wait for price to return to the zone
What is marked
BSL. The rally topped and price began to range. The line across that top marks the buy-side liquidity above it. This is the target, and it did not exist when the shift happened. It was set once the high had formed.
$$. The low of the earlier spike down, still untouched, just above the order block.
OB and protected low. Unchanged from slide 1.
The position. Entry at the top edge of the order block. Stop a little below the protected low. Target on the BSL line.
Why the plan is built this way
The order block is tall, so the stop cannot hide just beneath a thin zone as it did on gold. It goes under the protected low, which is also the bottom of the block. One level does both jobs: if it breaks, the order block has failed and the shift has failed.
Even with that wider stop, the distance from the top of the block to the BSL high is about 3.5 times the risk. The rally that tempted people to chase is the same rally that created the reward.
Rule to carry forward
Waiting with a plan means four things are written down before price returns: the entry price, the stop, the target, and what would cancel the order. If any one is missing, you are just watching.

entries.p: BTC/USD What Happens After the Sweep
entries.h: Price taps the zone, then reaches the target
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute Bitcoin chart after the trade. Price falls sharply from the range, through the dollar-sign low and deep into the order block, then reverses and rallies through the BSL high.
Slide 3 — result. “Price Taps the Zone, Then Reaches the Target.”
Step 3 · Fill, management and outcome
Price taps the zone, then reaches the target
What happened
Price fell out of the range fast. Several large bearish candles in a row, starting around 09:00 on the chart.
The $$ low was taken. Every stop under the earlier dip was triggered on the way down.
The order filled, and price kept going. Wicks reached more than halfway through the order block. The trade was in drawdown almost immediately.
The protected low held. Price never reached it. Two candles left long lower wicks inside the block, then buyers took over.
Target reached and exceeded. Price rallied straight back to the BSL high, went through it, and continued up to the dotted line above.
What to take from it
The wait was about nine hours. The shift came around midnight on the chart and the fill a little after 09:00.
This fill was deep. In the other three cases price only touched the near edge of the order block. Here it went well inside. A stop placed under the top half of the block would have been hit before the reversal.
The entry was into strong selling. The candles arriving at the order block were large and bearish. A limit order takes that trade without hesitation. A trader waiting to “see a reaction” would have entered much higher, or not at all.
A strict reading would call the drop a bearish shift. The $$ low was the higher low behind the last break up, and price traded below it. The post treats it as liquidity. What kept the long valid was the protected low underneath. That is the line to watch.
Price went beyond the target. Taking profit at the BSL left some of the move behind. That is the cost of a fixed target, and the plan was still met in full.
Rule to carry forward
Size the trade so that price trading through most of the order block does not worry you. The stop belongs under the protected low, and the position should be small enough that you can leave it there.

After a sweep and a shift, leave a buy limit at the order block with the stop under the protected low, and let price come back for the liquidity in front of it, however long that takes.

Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Buy limit at the top edge of the order block.
Placed after the MSS and left in place through the near miss and the rally.
The imbalance ends at the top of the block, so that edge is the first price a full pullback reaches.
Price went much deeper here. Entering at the top edge still worked because the stop was under the whole block.
A lower entry, say mid-block, would have filled too and paid more per unit of risk. It would have missed the three earlier cases. Choose one rule and keep it.
Stop loss
Below the protected low, plus a buffer.
The protected low is the sweep low (X) and also the bottom of the order block.
If it breaks, the liquidity sweep has been undone and the bullish shift is void.
The grey box extends slightly past the line. That gap is the buffer.
Do not tighten it to the middle of the block. This trade would have been stopped out before the reversal.
Take profit
The BSL line: the high made after the shift. About 3.5R.
No opposing supply zone is marked. The target is the stops above the most recent high.
The target was set after that high formed, not at the moment of the shift.
Price ran through it here. In GBP/JPY it only touched. Setting the order a few pips before the level covers both.
If you want to stay in for more, close most at the BSL and trail the rest. Decide before entry.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
While waiting: cancel only if the protected low breaks. A new high without you is not a reason to move the order up.
Re-measure when the target forms. Once price prints the high you will aim at, check the trade still pays at least 1:2 from the order block.
Once filled: expect drawdown inside the block. Do nothing unless the stop is hit.
Position size on Bitcoin
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the size.
Size in BTC = money at risk ÷ stop distance in dollars
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. A stop $400 away from entry gives 100 ÷ 400 = 0.25 BTC. At 1:3.5 the target pays about $350.
Check what 0.25 BTC is worth at the current price: it can be more than the account, which means leverage. The risk is still $100 only if the stop actually executes at its price. Bitcoin trades through weekends when liquidity is thin and stops can slip, and perpetual contracts charge funding while you wait in a position.

A long on Bitcoin that spells out the order of events behind every trade on this site. First liquidity is swept. Then structure shifts. Only then is there a zone worth buying. Here the sequence runs on the 4H for bias and again on the 1H for the entry.
