entries.h: The sequence, in three words
entries.t:
Chart: Line diagram. Price falls toward a higher-timeframe demand zone, bounces, then drops into the zone and sweeps the first low (X). It rallies above the bounce high (MSS), pulls back into a lower-timeframe demand zone and moves up.
Cover — “Sweep, Shift and Zone. The only sequence you need to know.”
The model
The sequence, in three words
Sweep. Price makes a low just above the HTF demand, bounces, then drops into the zone and takes that low (X). Buyers who entered on the first touch are stopped out here.
Shift. Price rallies and closes above the high of the bounce (MSS). The lower timeframe has turned.
Zone. The base of the leg that made the shift becomes the LTF demand. Price pulls back into it, and that is the entry.
Why the order matters
The caption describes the trader who gets the zone right and the order wrong. They buy when price first reaches HTF demand. That is before the sweep. Price drops a little more to take the low, their stop goes with it, and the move starts without them.
The same zone traded in the right order gives a different trade: the entry comes after the low is taken and the shift is confirmed, from a smaller zone with a stop under a low that has already been swept.
Rule to carry forward
Reaching the zone is step zero. The trade needs three events after that, in this order: a low is swept, structure shifts, price returns to the zone the shift left behind.

entries.h: 4H: the sequence gives the bias
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour Bitcoin chart. A sweep and rally out of a demand zone on the left, a high marked BSL, a sharp drop and range, then a wick sweeps the range lows (X) and the last candle closes above the previous high (MSS).
Slide 1 — “BTCUSD 4H – Bias.”
Step 1 · Bias
4H: the sequence gives the bias
What happened
An earlier sweep and rally. On the left, a long wick takes a low (the first X) inside the olive demand zone and price rallies hard out of it.
The rally tops out (BSL). The line across that high marks buy-side liquidity. It is the obvious draw above.
A sharp drop, then a range. One large bearish candle gives back most of the rally. Price then goes sideways for two days, leaving lows at a similar level.
The range lows are swept (second X). A push down runs under those lows and is bought back within the same candle.
MSS. The final candle closes above the most recent swing high. The 4H has completed sweep and shift.
Why this matters
The 4H now says two things: sell-side liquidity under the range has been taken, and structure has turned up. With the BSL high still untouched above, the bias is long and the target is known before the entry timeframe is opened.
Rule to carry forward
Take a long bias from the 4H only when both halves are present: a low swept and a close above the last swing high. Mark the nearest untouched high above as the draw.

entries.h: 1H: equal lows swept into demand, then the shift
entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour Bitcoin chart. After a rally and drop, price forms two equal lows (EQL) above a wide demand zone, then a wick sweeps them into the top of the zone and price rallies above the previous high (MSS).
Slide 2 — “1H – Confirmation.”
Step 2 · Confirmation
1H: equal lows swept into demand, then the shift
What happened
A wide demand zone sits below. The box labelled Demand is the base of the first rally, extended to the right.
Price made equal lows above it (EQL). Two lows roughly a day apart stopped at almost the same price, just over the zone. Each bounce encouraged buyers, and their stops sit under that double bottom.
The equal lows were swept into the zone. A drop ran through both lows and its wick dipped into the top of the demand before price turned.
MSS. The rally that followed closed above the previous swing high.
Why this matters
This is the cover drawing on a real chart. Price hovered above the zone and built liquidity. It then took that liquidity and tapped the zone in the same move. Anyone who bought either of the equal lows was stopped at the worst possible moment.
Rule to carry forward
Equal lows resting just above a demand zone are a target, not support. Wait for them to be run into the zone and for a 1H close above the last swing high before planning the entry.

entries.h: 1H: the zone the shift left behind
entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour Bitcoin chart with the long planned. After the shift price makes a high marked BSL and pulls back. A demand zone sits under an imbalance at the base of the shift. The entry is at the top of the zone, the stop under the sweep low and the target at the BSL line.
Slide 3 — “1H – Entry.”
Step 3 · Zone and order placement
1H: the zone the shift left behind
What is marked
X and the line beneath it. The sweep of the lows, and a line drawn from the sweep's own low. The post does not label that line. It is the level the stop sits under.
MSS. The break of the previous high.
IMB. The imbalance left by the rally, above the zone.
Demand. A narrow zone at the base of the leg that made the shift. This is the third word of the title.
BSL. After the shift price ran up and made a high. The line across it is the target.
A short line under the pullback. Price has come off the high and paused. The low of that pause is marked with an unlabelled line. It reads as liquidity sitting between price and the zone.
Why the entry is here
Entry is a buy limit at the top edge of the 1H demand. The stop goes below the sweep low, a little under the bottom of the zone. From entry to the BSL line is about 3.4 times that risk.
At the moment of this slide, price is far above the zone and has already made a new high. The plan is to wait for it to come back.
Rule to carry forward
The zone to trade is the one created by the shift, not the larger zone price was in when the shift happened. It is smaller, it gives a tighter stop, and it sits above a low that has already been swept.

entries.h: Result
entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour Bitcoin chart after the trade. A wick drops through the pullback low to the top of the demand zone, price bounces, forms a higher low above the zone, then rallies through the BSL line.
Slide 4 — “Result.”
Step 4 · Fill, management and outcome
Result
What happened
Price ranged at the pullback low. Several hours of small candles along the unlabelled line.
One wick took that low and tagged the zone. It reached just inside the top of the demand and closed well above. The buy limit filled on that wick.
A bounce, then a second dip. Price rallied, then drifted back down for several hours. It made a higher low and did not return to the zone.
Expansion. A run of large bullish candles carried price to the BSL line and through it.
What to take from it
The wait was about a day. On a 1H chart the shift and the fill were roughly 26 hours apart. The move to target took around 13 more.
The fill was a wick at the edge. A deeper order would not have filled.
Liquidity above the zone was taken first. The same behaviour as in the GBP/JPY, AUD/USD and first Bitcoin cases.
The second dip tested patience. For hours after the fill the trade gave back most of its early profit. Nothing structural had changed: the zone and the sweep low were intact.
Rule to carry forward
After the fill, the only levels that matter are the stop and the target. A slow drift back toward entry is not a signal.

entries.h: The whole trade as one sequence
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole trade as one sequence
The cover drawing is the picture. These are the same three steps, run twice.
| | On the 4H (bias) | On the 1H (entry)
| Sweep | The range lows are run by a wick | Equal lows are run into the demand zone
| Shift | 4H close above the last swing high | 1H close above the last swing high, leaving an imbalance
| Zone | Not traded directly. It tells you to look for longs | Demand at the base of the shift. Buy limit at its top edge
1 · BIAS
The 4H sweeps the lows of a two-day range and closes above the last swing high. The untouched high above is the draw.
2 · SWEEP
On the 1H, equal lows above demand are taken and the wick taps the zone.
3 · SHIFT
The 1H closes above the previous high. An imbalance and a narrow demand zone are left at the base.
4 · ZONE
About a day later, a wick clears the pullback low and tags the top of the 1H demand. The limit order fills.
5 · TARGET
After one more dip that holds above the zone, price expands through the BSL line. About 3.4R.
THE LOGIC IN ONE SENTENCE
Do not buy the zone when price reaches it. Buy the zone that is left after the low has been swept and structure has shifted.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Buy limit at the top edge of the 1H demand zone.
The zone is the base of the leg that made the 1H MSS, under the imbalance.
Place it once the shift is confirmed and leave it.
Only a wick reached the edge. A mid-zone order would have been missed.
Stop loss
Below the sweep low, plus a buffer.
The sweep low is the wick that took the equal lows. On the entry slide a line is drawn from it and the grey box ends just beneath.
It sits a little under the bottom of the demand zone, so the stop covers the zone and the low together.
If that low breaks, the sweep has been undone and the shift is void.
Take profit
The BSL line: the high above. About 3.4R.
On the 1H slides the line is drawn across the high price made after the shift.
The 4H slide also marks BSL at a high, so the bias chart and the entry chart point at the same area.
Price went through the level. Set the order a little before it regardless.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
While waiting: cancel if the sweep low breaks, or if price takes the BSL without filling you.
Once filled: hold through the retest. Move the stop only after a new 1H high and a confirmed higher low.
A day is a long time on Bitcoin. Check for scheduled news and for weekend gaps in liquidity while the order rests.
Position size on Bitcoin
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the size.
Size in BTC = money at risk ÷ stop distance in dollars
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. A stop $800 away from entry gives 100 ÷ 800 = 0.125 BTC. At 1:3.4 the target pays about $340.
A 1H zone usually means a wider stop in dollars than a 15m one, so the size is smaller for the same risk. Check the position's full value against your account: it may involve leverage, and stops can slip in thin markets.

entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Written for longs. For shorts, mirror it. A “no” at any step ends the process.
4H: has a low been swept and has price closed above the last swing high?Both. Then mark the nearest untouched high above as the draw.
1H: mark the demand zone below and the lows resting above it.Equal lows or a clean swing low just over the zone are the liquidity.
Sweep: have those lows been taken, into or onto the zone?Not yet means no trade yet, even if price is sitting on the zone.
Shift: has a 1H candle closed above the last swing high?It should leave an imbalance.
Zone: mark the demand at the base of the shift.Under the imbalance, above the sweep low. It must be untouched.
Does it pay at least 1:2 to the high above?Entry at the zone's top edge, stop under the sweep low, target just before the BSL.
Place the orders and wait.Size for 0.5–1% risk. On the 1H the wait can be a day or more.
Hold, then record it.Exit at target or stop. Note whether the sweep, the shift and the zone came in that order.

entries.h: When this setup should be skipped
entries.t:
Filters
When this setup should be skipped
Do not take it if
The steps are out of order: a shift with no sweep before it, or a zone with no shift.
The 4H has swept a low and not yet closed above a swing high.
The lows above the 1H zone are still intact.
The 1H demand has already been tapped since the shift.
The sweep low breaks.
The high above is closer than 1:2 from the zone.
This trade had all of these
4H sweep of the range lows and a 4H MSS.
1H equal lows swept into demand.
1H MSS with an imbalance.
An untouched 1H demand at the base of the shift.
A pullback low above the zone, taken on the fill.
A clear high about 3.4R away.
Keep this in proportion
“The only sequence you need to know” is the post's headline, not a guarantee. The sequence describes how these winning trades were built. It also appears before trades that fail: the low is swept, structure shifts, the zone is tapped, and price goes through it anyway. The sequence tells you when a trade is worth taking. Position size and the stop are what keep the failures small.

entries.h: 1H: a demand zone that broke structure
entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour GBP/AUD chart. A strong rally breaks structure (BoS) and leaves a demand zone at its base. Price tops out, gaps lower, and declines over the following day until a wick dips into the demand zone.
Slide 1 — “1h Timeframes.”
Step 1 · Map the higher timeframe
1H: a demand zone that broke structure
What happened
A rally broke structure (BoS). At the lower left, price closes above a prior high and then runs up strongly.
Demand is drawn at the base. The zone covers the small candles just before the impulse. That is where the buying that broke structure began.
Price topped and came all the way back. Two highs, then a gap lower between sessions, then a steady decline. Almost the entire rally was retraced.
The zone was tapped. One wick dipped well into the demand zone and was rejected. Price then sat just above the zone for several hours.
Why this zone is worth trading
It caused a break of structure.
This is the first return to it.
It is at the very bottom of the leg, so deep in discount.
The pullback into it is long and steep, though. On the 1H there is no sign yet that the selling has stopped. That is the 15m's job.
Rule to carry forward
Start on the 1H. Find the zone that produced the last break of structure, check it is fresh and in discount, and wait for price to reach it. Then change timeframe.

entries.h: 15m: tap, range, sweep, shift
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/AUD chart. Price drops into the 1H demand zone and bounces, ranges for hours, sweeps the range low (X) at the top of the zone, then one large bullish candle closes above the bounce high (MSS).
Slide 2 — “15m Timeframes.” The large box is the 1H demand.
Step 2 · Sweep and shift
15m: tap, range, sweep, shift
What happened
First tap of the 1H zone. A hard drop takes price into the demand and it bounces sharply. The high of that bounce is the level the MSS line is drawn from.
A nine-hour range. Price drifts sideways and slightly down above the zone. Lows form along the bottom of the range.
The range low is swept (X). A wick runs under the lowest of those lows, reaches the top of the 1H zone and closes back up.
MSS. The very next move is one large bullish candle that closes above the bounce high. Nine hours of range is cleared in fifteen minutes.
Why this matters
The first tap at 10:30 looked like the entry and was not. The bounce it produced went nowhere for nine hours and price came back for the lows. The trade only became valid once those lows were taken and the bounce high was broken with displacement.
The two events arrived back to back: sweep, then shift on the next push. That is as clean as the sequence gets.
Rule to carry forward
After the first reaction from a 1H zone, mark the bounce high and the lows that form afterwards. The signal is a sweep of those lows followed by a 15m close above the bounce high.

entries.h: 15m: the demand the shift left behind
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/AUD chart just after the shift. A 15-minute demand zone is drawn at the base of the displacement candle, with an imbalance marked above it.
Slide 3 — “15m Timeframes.” The zone is marked.
Step 3 · Mark the zone
15m: the demand the shift left behind
What is marked
15m Demand. A box at the base of the displacement candle, covering the last small candles before it. It sits just above the 1H zone.
IMB. The displacement candle left an imbalance directly above the 15m demand.
The sweep low. The X wick sits a little below the bottom of the 15m demand box.
Why this is the zone
It is the origin of the candle that broke structure, it formed immediately after the sweep, and nothing lies beneath it except the low that has already been taken. By the checks on the inducement page, this is the real zone.
Rule to carry forward
As soon as the MSS candle closes, draw the demand at its base and note the imbalance above. That box is where the limit order goes.

entries.h: 15m: inducement above, liquidity target overhead
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/AUD chart with the long planned. Price has rallied above the shift and left an inducement low (IDM). The entry is at the top of the 15-minute demand, the stop under the sweep low and the target at the BSL line across the earlier high.
Slide 4 — “15m Timeframes.” The order is planned.
Step 4 · Plan the order
15m: inducement above, liquidity target overhead
What is marked
BSL. A line across the high on the far left, where the sell-off into the 1H zone began. Buy-side liquidity rests above it. This is the target.
IDM. After the shift, price paused and made a small low before pushing higher. That low is the inducement. Early buyers have stops under it.
IMB. The imbalance sits between the inducement and the 15m demand.
The position. Entry at the top edge of the 15m demand. Stop under the sweep low. Target on the BSL line.
Why the plan is built this way
For price to reach the entry it must first take the inducement low and fill the imbalance. So the fill comes after the early longs are out. The stop sits under the low that started the whole move, slightly beyond the bottom of the zone. From entry to the BSL is about 2.9 times that risk.
Rule to carry forward
The target for a long out of a pullback is the high the pullback started from. Mark it before the entry. If it is less than twice the risk away, there is no trade.

entries.h: Result
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/AUD chart after the trade. Price pulls back through the inducement low and the imbalance, touches the top of the 15-minute demand, then rallies to the BSL line and wicks through it.
Slide 5 — “Result.”
Step 5 · Fill, management and outcome
Result
What happened
Price pulled back from the post-shift high.
The inducement low was taken and the imbalance filled.
Price touched the top of the 15m demand. It did not travel into the zone. The limit order filled at the edge.
A steady climb. Price rallied, paused once below the target, then pushed on.
Target reached. Price hit the BSL line and wicked through it.
What to take from it
This was the quickest of the cases. About three hours from shift to fill and about three more to target.
The fill was a touch. Again, only the near edge of the zone was reached.
The inducement was taken first. The same pattern as AUD/USD, on a shorter clock.
A calendar marker sits on the time axis close to when the target was reached. The post does not comment on it. It is a reminder to check what is scheduled while a trade is open.
Rule to carry forward
The sequence does not have a fixed duration. The steps and their order are the plan. The clock is not.

A schematic of the 15m sequence, not a copy of the chart. Read it left to right.
1 · FIRST TAP
Price falls from the high into the 1H demand and bounces. Not an entry. The bounce high becomes the MSS level.

After a nine-hour range, a wick runs the range low at the top of the 1H zone.

One candle closes above the bounce high. It leaves an imbalance and the 15m demand at its base.

At a 1H demand that broke structure, wait for the 15m to sweep and shift, buy the zone that shift leaves, and target the high the pullback came from.

Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Buy limit at the top edge of the 15m demand.
The zone is the base of the displacement candle, under the imbalance.
Price only touched the edge. A deeper order would not have filled.
Buys fill on the ask. GBP/AUD has a wide spread, so add it to the limit price.
Stop loss
Below the sweep low (X), plus a buffer.
The sweep low sits slightly under the bottom of the 15m demand. The grey box ends at about that wick.
If it breaks, the sweep is undone and the shift is void.
It is not under the 1H zone. That would be roughly twice as wide on this chart.
Crosses like GBP/AUD move quickly. Leave a few pips beyond the wick.
Take profit
The BSL line: the high before the drop. About 2.9R.
It is the 15m high the sell-off into the 1H zone started from.
No opposing supply zone is marked. The target is liquidity.
Price wicked through the level. Set the order a few pips before it regardless.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
While waiting: cancel if a 15m candle closes below the 15m demand, or if price reaches the BSL without filling you.
Once filled: leave the stop until price clears the post-shift high and prints a higher low.
News: check the calendar for GBP and AUD releases before leaving an order or a position overnight.
Position size
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the lot size.
Lots = money at risk ÷ (stop in pips × pip value per lot)
On GBP/AUD one standard lot moves 10 Australian dollars per pip. In US dollars that is 10 × the AUD/USD rate, for example $6.50 at 0.6500.
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. Stop of 25 pips at $6.50 per pip per lot gives 100 ÷ (25 × 6.50) ≈ 0.62 lots. At 1:2.9 the target pays about $290.

entries.h: 1H: an uptrend pulls back into its order block
entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour GBP/JPY chart. Price climbs through three breaks of structure to a peak, then falls back. A 1-hour order block is drawn at the base of the first leg. A wick at the right dips under an earlier pullback low, marked X, into the top of the order block, and price bounces.
Slide 1 — “1h Timeframe.”
Step 1 · Higher-timeframe bias and zone
1H: an uptrend pulls back into its order block
What happened
Three breaks of structure upward. Each BoS is a close above the previous high. The 1H trend is up.
The 1H order block. A wide box at the base of the leg that made the first break.
A full pullback. From the peak, price gives back the whole of the last leg in about a day.
The sweep (X). A wick drops under an earlier pullback low, reaches the top of the order block, and closes back up.
Why this matters
Three things line up at one price: an uptrend, an order block that started it, and a low just above that block whose stops have now been taken. That is the place to look for a long. It is not yet a reason to buy. The pullback was steep, and a 1H wick alone does not show that it is over.
Rule to carry forward
In a 1H uptrend, mark the order block and the lows sitting above it. When a wick takes one of those lows and reaches the block, go down to the 15m.

entries.h: 15m: a shift up, then a return to the 15m order block
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/JPY chart. Price drops from a flat range into the 1-hour order block, where a wick is marked X. It rallies strongly and closes above the range high (MSS). A 15-minute order block is drawn partway up the rally. Price ranges at the top, then falls back, and a long wick reaches into the 15-minute order block.
Slide 2 — “15m Timeframe.” The lower box is the top of the 1H OB.
Step 2 · Middle timeframe
15m: a shift up, then a return to the 15m order block
What happened
The drop into the 1H OB. From a quiet range, price falls hard. The wick marked X is the 1H sweep seen up close.
The rally. A run of bullish candles takes back the whole drop.
MSS. Price closes above the high the drop started from.
The 15m order block. A box partway up the rally, at the small candles before the strongest push.
The return. After a range at the top, price drops. It takes a small low and one long wick reaches into the 15m OB.
Why this matters
The 15m confirms what the 1H suggested: the sweep was followed by a shift. On most pages of this site, the entry would now be a limit at the 15m order block. This trade goes one step further and asks the 5m for the same proof inside that block. The reward is a smaller stop.
Rule to carry forward
After the 15m shift, mark the 15m order block. When price comes back to it, drop to the 5m and look for a sweep and a shift there.

entries.h: 5m: sweep and shift inside the 15m order block
entries.t:
Chart: 5-minute GBP/JPY chart with the long planned. A BSL line runs from the high at the left. Price drops, makes a low, and a later candle sweeps it (X) with a long wick into the 15-minute order block; the wick low is labelled SSL. Price then closes above a prior high (MSS), leaving an imbalance and a 5-minute order block. The position box has its entry at the top of the 5-minute order block, its stop just under the SSL line and its target at the BSL line.
Slide 3 — “5m Timeframe.” The lower-left box is the 15m OB.
Step 3 · Confirmation and plan
5m: sweep and shift inside the 15m order block
What happened
The high at the left. The top of the 15m range. The BSL line is drawn from it.
The drop. Just before 02:00 price falls away from that high and makes a low.
The sweep (X), a little after 03:00. One candle takes that low. Its long wick goes into the 15m order block. The wick low is labelled SSL.
MSS, about 03:20–03:30. Price closes above the last 5m high. The move leaves an imbalance (IMB).
The 5m order block. A box from the base of the MSS move down to the sweep low.
The position box
Entry: the top edge of the 5m OB.
Stop: just under the SSL line, the low of the sweep wick. That is inside the 15m OB, not under it.
Target: the BSL line. About 2.5 times the stop.
The 5m order block is tall because it includes the whole sweep wick. That makes the stop wide for a 5m entry and is why the ratio is 2.5 and not higher.

entries.h: Result: two more sweeps, then the target
entries.t:
Chart: 5-minute GBP/JPY result. After the shift price rallies, then drops sharply. It sweeps a small low (X) and reaches the top of the 5-minute order block, filling the long. It chops, then dips again, sweeping another low (X) about halfway into the order block. It then rallies, pauses, and one large candle reaches the BSL line.
Slide 4 — “Result.”
Step 4 · Result
Result: two more sweeps, then the target
What happened
A rally without a fill. After the shift price ran up until about 04:30. It stopped short of the BSL.
A sharp drop, about 04:40. It left a small low.
First sweep and the fill, about 05:10. That low was taken (X) and price reached the top of the 5m OB. The buy limit filled, roughly an hour and three quarters after the shift.
An hour of chop. Price moved sideways just above the block.
Second sweep, about 06:15. One candle took the low of the chop (X) and went about halfway into the 5m OB. The stop was not reached.
The rally. Up until about 07:00, a pause for an hour with one sharp dip, then a single large candle to the BSL a little after 08:00.
What to take from it
The trade was underwater by about half its stop an hour after the fill. That is normal for an edge entry.
Each dip took a low that had just formed. On the 5m, liquidity builds and is taken within an hour.
A stop tucked just inside the block would have been hit at 06:15. The one under the sweep low held.

entries.h: The whole trade on one page
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole trade on one page
Chart: Cover slide: GBPJPY, showing the finished 5-minute long from the order block to the BSL line.
Cover — “GBPJPY.” The finished trade.
The same three steps repeat on each timeframe: a sweep, a reaction, a zone. Each zone sits inside the one above it.
| | 1H | 15m | 5m
| Job | Direction and location | First confirmation | Entry
| Sweep | An earlier pullback low, into the 1H OB | The same wick, seen up close | A 5m low, into the 15m OB
| Shift | None needed. The trend is already up | MSS above the high before the drop | MSS above the last 5m high
| Zone | 1H OB | 15m OB | 5m OB
| Used for | Where to start looking | Where to drop to the 5m | The limit order and the stop
1 · BIAS AND LOCATION
The 1H is in an uptrend. A pullback sweeps a low and taps the 1H order block.
2 · 15m CONFIRMATION
The 15m rallies from the tap and closes above the high before the drop. It leaves a 15m order block.
3 · 5m SWEEP AND SHIFT
Price returns. A 5m low is swept with a wick into the 15m order block, then the 5m shifts up with an imbalance.
4 · ENTRY
Buy limit at the top of the 5m order block. It fills after a small low above it is swept. A second dip goes halfway into the block and holds.
5 · TARGET
Price returns to the high the drop came from. About 2.5R, roughly three hours after the fill.
THE LOGIC IN ONE SENTENCE
In a 1H uptrend at the 1H order block, wait for the 15m to shift, then buy the 5m order block that forms when price returns to the 15m one.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Buy limit at the top edge of the 5m OB.
The block runs from the base of the 5m MSS move down to the sweep low.
The first touch filled an order at the edge. The second dip, an hour later, went about halfway in.
Buys fill on the ask. GBP/JPY has a wide spread, so allow for it in the limit price.
Stop loss
Below the 5m sweep low (the SSL line), plus a buffer.
The grey box ends just under the SSL line.
If that low breaks, the 5m sweep is undone and the shift is void.
It sits inside the 15m OB. The wider alternative is under the 15m OB. It brings the ratio down to about 1:2 on this chart.
GBP/JPY moves fast. Leave a few pips beyond the wick.
Take profit
The BSL line: the high before the drop. About 2.5R.
It is the top of the 15m range, where the fall into the 15m OB began.
The first rally after the shift stopped short of it. The level was still untouched when the order filled.
Price wicked through it. Set the order a few pips before the line.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
While waiting: cancel if price reaches the BSL without filling you, or if a 5m candle closes below the SSL line.
Once filled: leave the stop alone. A stop moved to break-even during the first hour would have been hit by the 06:15 dip.
Time of day: the axis runs from 01:00 to 09:00 and the slides do not say which timezone. Check the spread at the hour you trade. It widens in quiet hours.
News: check the calendar for GBP and JPY releases before leaving an order or a position open.
Position size
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the lot size.
Lots = money at risk ÷ (stop in pips × pip value per lot)
On GBP/JPY one standard lot moves ¥1,000 per pip. In dollars that is 1,000 ÷ the USD/JPY rate, for example about $6.67 at 150.00.
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. Stop of 20 pips at $6.67 per pip per lot gives 100 ÷ (20 × 6.67) ≈ 0.75 lots. At 1:2.5 the target pays about $250. The 20 pips is an illustration. The slides show no prices.

entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Written for longs. For shorts, mirror it. A “no” at any step ends the process.
1H: is structure breaking upward?Mark the order block under the trend and the lows above it. Set an alert at the block.
Has a wick swept one of those lows and reached the 1H OB?Open the 15m.
15m: has price closed above the high the drop came from?That is the 15m MSS. Draw the 15m OB inside the rally.
Mark the high price pulls back from.That is the BSL and the target.
Has price come back to the 15m OB?Open the 5m.
5m: is a low swept into the 15m OB, and does a candle then close above the last 5m high?That is the 5m MSS. It should leave an imbalance.
Draw the 5m OB from the base of that move to the sweep low.Buy limit at its top edge. Stop under the sweep low. Target the BSL.
Does it pay at least 1:2?If not, skip it.
Size, place, hold, record.Risk 0.5–1%. Exit at target or stop. Screenshot the 1H, 15m and 5m.

entries.h: When this setup should be skipped
entries.t:
Filters
When this setup should be skipped
Do not take it if
The 1H is not in an uptrend, or a 1H candle closes below the 1H OB.
The 15m has not shifted up from the 1H OB.
Price has not returned to the 15m OB. A 5m pattern above it is inducement.
The 5m breaks up without first sweeping a low.
The 5m break has no imbalance.
The spread is a large part of the stop. On a 5m entry it can be.
The high above is closer than 1:2.
High-impact GBP or JPY news is due while the order rests.
This trade had all of these
A 1H uptrend with three breaks of structure.
A sweep of a low into the 1H order block.
A 15m MSS and a 15m order block.
A 5m sweep and MSS inside the 15m order block, with an imbalance.
A low above the entry taken before the fill.
An untouched high about 2.5R away.
Keep this in proportion
A 5m entry gives a smaller stop in pips, which means a larger position for the same risk. Spread and slippage then take a bigger share of each trade, and a few pips of noise decide more outcomes. This trade dipped halfway to its stop before it worked. If you are still building consistency, the 15m order block entry is the slower and more forgiving version of the same idea.

entries.p: GBP/JPY Strong Structure Starts With a Sweep
entries.h: Higher timeframe: break down, then sweep the low
entries.t:
Chart: Higher-timeframe GBP/JPY chart. Two breaks of structure downward, a descending trendline of highs marked with dollar signs, then a long wick below the last low marked X and a strong recovery.
Slide 1 — higher timeframe. “Price breaks structure down, then sweeps the low.”
Step 1 · Context and liquidity
Higher timeframe: break down, then sweep the low
What happened
Structure was bearish. Two BoS labels mark two lower lows. Anyone reading structure alone is looking for shorts.
The highs line up on a trendline ($$). Each lower high sits on the dashed line. Sellers trail their stops above it and breakout buyers wait there. That is buy-side liquidity building up overhead.
The second low was swept (X). One candle drove far below the last BoS low and was rejected. Nearly all of that move is wick.
Price recovered the whole breakdown. The candles that follow are bullish and carry price back up into the middle of the range. The slide ends with another long lower wick, which matters later.
Why this matters
The sell-side has been used. Stops under the low are gone. There is less reason for price to go back down there.
The buy-side is untouched. The trendline highs and the old high above them are still loaded. Price tends to travel from liquidity that has been taken toward liquidity that has not.
The sweep is a warning to sellers, not yet a buy signal. Higher-timeframe structure is still bearish on this slide. The case for a long has to be proven on the lower timeframe.
Rule to carry forward
Before trusting any break of structure, ask what was swept just before it. For a long, a higher-timeframe low must have been run and rejected, with untouched liquidity above to aim at.
How this differs from the other two cases
In USD/JPY and XAU/USD the higher timeframe had already shifted in the trade's direction. Here it had not. This is a reversal taken off a sweep, against two higher-timeframe breaks. That makes the 15m confirmation in the next step more important, not less.

entries.p: GBP/JPY Strong Structure Starts With a Sweep
entries.h: 15m: after the sweep, structure breaks up
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/JPY chart. A sharp drop through the higher-timeframe low, a second lower low marked X, then a rally that closes above the bounce high (MSS). An order block is marked below, with a wick low marked as liquidity above it.
Slide 2 — 15m chart. “After the sweep, price breaks structure to the upside.”
Step 2 · Confirmation
15m: after the sweep, structure breaks up
What happened
One large candle broke the higher-timeframe low. The BoS line on the left is that low. Price fell straight through it.
The sweep had two parts (X). Price bounced, then dropped again and went slightly below the first spike's low before turning. What looked like a single wick on the higher timeframe is a double low on the 15m, with the second low running the first.
MSS. The rally closed above the high of the bounce between the two lows. That is the lower high that led to the final low, so breaking it ends the 15m downtrend.
An order block was left behind. The OB box marks the last bearish candles before the leg that broke structure.
A wick low sits above the OB ($$). During the range at the top, one candle spiked down and recovered. Its low is marked as liquidity. Buyers who entered early have stops under it.
Why this matters
This is the sequence in the post's title. Liquidity was taken on the higher timeframe, and only then did the 15m break upward. A 15m break without that sweep would just be a bounce inside a downtrend.
The $$ mark is worth noticing before the trade is on. Unswept liquidity between price and the order block tells you two things: price has a reason to come down to the OB, and it will probably hunt those stops first.
Rule to carry forward
After a higher-timeframe sweep, wait for a 15m close above the lower high that produced the final low. Then mark the order block and any lows sitting between it and current price. Those lows are the path to your entry.

entries.p: GBP/JPY Strong Structure Starts With a Sweep
entries.h: 15m: wait for the return to the order block
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/JPY chart with the long planned. After the MSS price makes a further break of structure up to the trendline, then starts falling toward an order block with an imbalance above it. The target is the buy-side liquidity line at the top.
Slide 3 — 15m chart with the order planned. “Wait for price to return to the order block.”
Step 3 · Refinement and order placement
15m: wait for the return to the order block
What is marked
BoS after the MSS. Price made one more higher high before pulling back. The shift was followed through, which is a second confirmation.
That high touched the trendline ($$). Price reached the descending line of highs and turned down without breaking it. The liquidity above the line is still there.
IMB. An imbalance left by the rally sits directly on top of the order block.
OB. The same block as slide 2, drawn from the origin of the leg that broke structure.
$$ below price. The wick low from slide 2. Price is now heading toward it.
BSL. A horizontal line from an older high, off the left of the chart. Buy-side liquidity rests above it. The top of the blue box is on this line.
Why the entry is here
Entry is a buy limit at the top edge of the order block. To get there price has to take the $$ low and fill the imbalance, so the fill comes after early longs have been stopped out, not before.
The stop is drawn well below the bottom of the OB box. It clears the wicks of the swing low that the breaking leg started from. From entry, the distance up to the BSL line is about 3.8 times that risk.
Rule to carry forward
Do not buy the pullback while liquidity still sits between price and your order block. Leave the limit order at the OB and let price come through those lows to reach it.

entries.p: GBP/JPY Strong Structure Starts With a Sweep
entries.h: Result
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/JPY chart after the trade. Price sweeps two sets of lows above the order block, wicks into the top of the block, then rallies sharply to the buy-side liquidity line.
Slide 4 — result. “Price moves to the liquidity above.”
Step 4 · Management and outcome
Result
What happened
The $$ low was taken. Price fell from the trendline and ran the wick low. The first dashed line marks it.
Price stalled and built new lows. For several hours it ranged just above the order block, printing a cluster of lows at nearly the same price. The second dashed line marks them. More stops, even closer to the OB.
One wick swept those lows and tapped the OB. Around 02:00 on the chart a single candle dipped through the cluster, touched the top edge of the order block and closed back above. The buy limit filled on that wick.
Expansion. Price rallied almost without pause, through the trendline liquidity.
Target reached. A wick touched the BSL line and price pulled back from it immediately.
What to take from it
The wait was long. The shift happened around 13:30 on the chart and the fill came around 02:00 the next day. Roughly twelve hours with a resting order. The move to target then took a little over an hour.
Two stop hunts came before the entry. Anyone who bought the first dip, or the range lows, was taken out just before the move. The order block sat below both.
The fill was shallow, for the third case in a row. Price only reached the near edge of the OB.
The target was hit by a wick. Price tagged the BSL line and reversed. A take profit placed a few pips beyond the line would not have filled.
Rule to carry forward
When the target is a liquidity level, place the take profit a few pips before it. Price needs only to touch the stops there. It owes you nothing beyond that.

A schematic of the 15m sequence, not a copy of the chart. Read it left to right.
1 · SWEEP THE HTF LOW

2 · SHIFT

The logic in one sentence
After a higher-timeframe low is swept and the 15m breaks up, buy the order block once the lows above it have been cleared, and take profit just before the untouched highs.

Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Written for longs, as in this trade. For shorts, mirror it: highs for lows, sell-side for buy-side. A “no” at any step ends the process.
On the higher timeframe, mark the last swing low and the liquidity above.Trendline highs, equal highs and old highs are the buy-side. Set an alert just under the swing low.
Was the low swept and rejected?You want a wick below the low and a close back above it. A full-bodied close below with follow-through is a breakdown, not a sweep.
Is there untouched liquidity above to aim at?If the highs have already been run, there is no target and no trade.

Place the orders and wait.Buy limit, stop and target together, sized for 0.5–1% risk. The wait can be many hours.
Manage by structure, then record it.Cancel on a 15m close below the OB. Hold to target or stop. Screenshot the higher timeframe and the 15m.

entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour GBP/USD chart. A high is swept (X), then one large bearish candle breaks below the prior low (BoS). Price makes a low, then a higher low, with a dashed line marked with dollar signs under the two lows. Price bounces back up but stays below the high.
Slide 1 — “1H - Price breaks structure down, then bounces back up.”
Step 1 · Higher-timeframe bias
1H: structure breaks down, then a bounce
What happened
A high was swept (X). Before the drop, a wick ran above an earlier 1H high and failed. The line across the top marks the high that was left.
BoS down. One large bearish candle, around 21:00, closed below the prior low.
Two lows. Price made a low, bounced, and made a higher low around 02:00. The dashed line with $$$ joins them. Stops are resting under both.
The bounce. A large bullish candle from the second low, then a slower climb. Price stays below the high.
Why this matters
The 1H is bearish. The last structural event is a break down that came straight after a sweep of a high. The bounce is a pullback inside a bearish leg until price closes above that high.
The rising lows with $$$ are trendline liquidity. They give a short somewhere to aim.
Rule to carry forward
After a 1H break of structure down, treat the next rally as a pullback. Look for a short where the drop began, not for a long.

entries.h: 15m: the rally reaches supply and fails
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/USD chart. A supply zone is drawn where the drop began. Price falls, bases, breaks structure up (BoS) and rallies. Two highs of the rally are swept (X, X), the second by a wick inside the supply zone. A large bearish candle then closes below the last low of the rally (MSS).
Slide 2 — “15m - Price rallies into supply, then shifts structure down.”
Step 2 · Sweep and shift
15m: the rally reaches supply and fails
What happened
Supply is drawn at the origin of the drop. The box covers the last candles before the 21:00 sell-off that made the 1H BoS.
The 15m turned bullish. After the lows, price broke a small high (the dotted BoS) and rallied from about 02:00. Each pullback held. On this chart alone it looks like an uptrend.
First sweep (X), about 04:00. A high of the rally is taken and price dips.
Second sweep (X), about 05:30. Price pushes above the next high and a wick reaches well into the supply zone. It does not close there.
MSS, about 06:00. One large bearish candle closes below the last low of the rally.
Why this matters
The post describes it from the buyer's side: “Most traders saw a breakout and enter before the candle closed.” Those buyers bought inside 1H-bearish supply, at a high that had just been taken. Their stops sat under the last low. The MSS candle ran straight through them.
The sweep happened inside the supply zone. The inducement page makes the same point for longs: the sweep and shift have to happen at the zone.
Rule to carry forward
When a rally reaches supply, mark its last higher low. A sweep of a high inside the zone, followed by a 15m close below that low, is the signal. A wick into the zone on its own is not.

entries.h: 15m: the new supply, the stop and the target
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/USD chart with the short planned. A new, smaller supply zone is drawn below the old one, at the candles before the shift. A short dashed line with dollar signs sits just under it. The position box has its entry at the bottom of the new supply, its stop just above it and its target at the low marked Target.
Slide 3 — “15m - Wait for the confirmation. Enter from the new supply, target the low.”
Step 3 · Plan the trade
15m: the new supply, the stop and the target
What is marked
The new supply. A smaller box under the old zone. It covers the candles just before the bearish candle that made the MSS.
$$$ under the new supply. A short dashed line just below its bottom edge. I read it as the highs price is expected to make there before it reaches the zone.
The dotted line above. The high of the sweep wick.
Target. A line at the 02:00 low, the upper end of the $$$ trendline.
The position box. Entry at the bottom edge of the new supply. Stop just above its top edge. Target at the low.
Reading the box
The target is about 3.8 times the stop. The stop is above the new supply zone. It is below the sweep high, which is the dotted line. That is the tight version of the stop and it is what makes the ratio this large.
The target is the nearer of the two lows. The lowest low, from about 22:00, is further down and is not used.
Rule to carry forward
After the MSS candle closes, draw the supply at the candles it launched from. Sell limit at its bottom edge, stop above it, target the first clean low below.

entries.h: Result: filled within the hour, target an hour later
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute GBP/USD result. Price bounces after the shift, a wick enters the new supply zone and fills the short. Price falls, bounces briefly, and one large bearish candle reaches the Target line at the low.
Slide 4 — “price reaches the target.”
Step 4 · Result
Result: filled within the hour, target an hour later
What happened
A small bounce. After the MSS candle price climbed back for two or three candles.
The fill, a little before 07:00. The highs under the zone were taken and a wick went about a third of the way into the new supply.
The drop. Price fell, bounced once for a couple of candles, then one very large bearish candle around 08:00 reached the target.
The target was only just passed. The wick ends slightly below the line.
What to take from it
The wait from shift to fill was under an hour. From fill to target was a little over an hour.
The wick into the zone stopped short of the top edge, so the tight stop held.
A US flag sits on the time axis at 10:00. The trade was finished before it.

entries.h: The whole trade on one page
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole trade on one page
Chart: Cover slide: GBP/USD Simple Confirmation Entry, a close-up of the 15-minute rally into supply, the two sweeps, the shift, the new supply and the finished short.
Cover — “GBP/USD Simple Confirmation Entry.” A close-up of the last few hours.
1 · BIAS
The 1H sweeps a high and breaks structure down. The bounce that follows is a pullback.
2 · LOCATION
The 15m supply where the drop began. The rally climbs into it.
3 · SWEEP
Two highs of the rally are taken. The second wick reaches into the supply and fails.
4 · SHIFT
A large bearish candle closes below the rally's last low. It leaves a new, smaller supply.
5 · ENTRY AND TARGET
Price returns to the new supply within the hour and fills the sell limit. It reaches the low about an hour later. About 3.8R.
THE LOGIC IN ONE SENTENCE
In a 1H downtrend, let the rally reach supply and take its highs, wait for the 15m to shift down, and sell the new supply toward the low.

entries.h: The breakout buyer and the trader who waited
entries.t:
Same chart, two outcomes
The breakout buyer and the trader who waited
The post tells this trade as a story about two people. Put side by side, the difference is what each one looked at.
| | Chased the breakout | Waited for confirmation
| Timeframe read | 15m only: higher highs and higher lows | 1H first: structure broken down, price bouncing
| The supply zone | Not marked | Marked in advance as the place to look for a short
| The push above the high | A breakout. Bought before the candle closed | A sweep, if the candle fails to close there
| Entry | Market buy at the high | Sell limit at the new supply, after the MSS
| Stop | Under the last low, which the MSS candle ran through | Above the new supply
| Outcome | Stopped out | Target at the low, about 3.8R
The post's wording for the first trader: “Buyers were trapped, liquidity above was taken and their stops pushed price down even faster.”
This is the confirmation model from the entry models page on a real chart: tap of the higher zone, sweep, shift, then an entry at the smaller zone.
The aggressive entry would also have worked here
A sell limit at the bottom of the old supply with a stop above it would have filled on the 05:30 wick and reached the same target. It needs a wider stop and gives no evidence beforehand. The post's point is about the buyer who chased, not about that seller.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Sell limit at the bottom edge of the new 15m supply.
The zone is the group of candles just before the bearish candle that made the MSS.
The slides mark $$$ just under the zone. Do not sell there. Let those highs be taken.
A wick went about a third of the way into the zone. An order at the edge filled.
Sells fill on the bid, so no spread needs adding to the limit price.
Stop loss
Just above the new supply, plus spread and a buffer.
The grey box ends slightly above the top of the new supply, below the sweep high.
If price closes back above the zone, the shift has failed.
Buy stops trigger on the ask. Add the spread to the stop price.
The safer alternative is above the sweep high, the dotted line. It is wider and brings the ratio down.
Take profit
The Target line: the 02:00 low. About 3.8R.
It is the low the rally into supply started from.
It is the nearer of the two lows on the $$$ line. The lower one is left alone.
Price passed the line by very little. Set the order a few pips above it.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
While waiting: cancel if price reaches the target without filling you, or if a 15m candle closes above the new supply.
Once filled: leave the stop alone through the first bounce. That bounce is on the chart, about halfway down.
News: the axis shows a US event at 10:00. If the trade is still open shortly before a release like that, decide beforehand whether you close or hold.
Position size
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the lot size.
Lots = money at risk ÷ (stop in pips × pip value per lot)
On GBP/USD one standard lot moves $10 per pip.
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. Stop of 10 pips gives 100 ÷ (10 × 10) = 1.0 lot. At 1:3.8 the target pays about $380. The 10 pips is an illustration. The slides show no prices.

entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Written for shorts. For longs, mirror it. A “no” at any step ends the process.
1H: has structure broken down?A close below the prior low, ideally after a high was swept. Bias is short.
15m: draw the supply where that drop began.The last candles before the sell-off. Set an alert at its bottom edge.
Mark the lows under the bounce.The low the rally starts from is the target.
Price rallies into the supply. Do not buy the rally and do not sell yet.Mark each high it makes and its last higher low.
Is a high swept at or inside the supply?A push above the high that fails to close there.
Does a 15m candle close below the last higher low?That is the MSS. It should be a large, fast candle.
Draw the new supply at the candles before that candle.Sell limit at its bottom edge. Stop above it. Target the low.
Does it pay at least 1:2?If not, skip it.
Size, place, hold, record.Risk 0.5–1%. Exit at target or stop. Screenshot the 1H and the 15m.

entries.h: When this setup should be skipped
entries.t:
Filters
When this setup should be skipped
Do not take it if
The 1H has not broken structure down, or has closed back above the high.
The rally has not reached the supply zone.
A 15m candle closes above the supply zone.
The 15m breaks down without first sweeping a high.
The break is a slow drift, not a displacement candle.
Price has already reached the low before the order can fill.
The low is closer than 1:2.
High-impact GBP or USD news is due while the order rests.
This trade had all of these
A 1H break of structure down after a swept high.
A 15m supply at the origin of that drop.
Two highs swept, the second inside the supply.
A 15m MSS on one large candle.
A new supply tapped within the hour.
A clear low about 3.8R away.
Keep this in proportion
This trade was fast and clean, and the tight stop was never tested. That makes it a good illustration and a poor guide to how often it works. A stop just above a small 15m zone is hit more often than one above the sweep high. The 3.8R comes from accepting that. Backtest both stops before choosing.

entries.h: 1H: a low is swept, then structure shifts up
entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour USD/JPY chart. Price rises, then drops sharply. A long wick runs below an earlier low (X) and closes back above it. A smaller low is swept (X), price rallies and closes above the high the drop started from (MSS).
Slide 1 — “1h Timeframes.”
Step 1 · Higher-timeframe bias
1H: a low is swept, then structure shifts up
What happened
A sharp drop. Two large bearish candles erase the previous rally.
The old low is swept (the long X line). A long wick runs under the low at the left of the chart. The candle closes back above it.
A second, smaller sweep (the short X). A few candles later a minor low is taken and rejected.
MSS. Price rallies and closes above the high the drop began from.
Why this matters
The drop looked bearish. It took the stops under the old low and then failed to hold below it. When the 1H then closed above the starting high, the whole drop became a sweep. The bias for the lower timeframes is long.
Rule to carry forward
A 1H sweep of a low followed by a 1H close above the high before the drop gives a long bias. Do not buy yet. Go down a timeframe and find where that move started.

entries.h: 30m: the demand at the origin of the shift
entries.t:
Chart: 30-minute USD/JPY chart of the same move. After the drop and sweep, a small low is swept (X), then a large bullish candle leaves an imbalance and a 30-minute demand zone at its base. Rising lows above the zone are marked with dollar signs. Price breaks the high before the drop (MSS), pulls back, and breaks higher again (BoS).
Slide 2 — “30m Timeframes.” The same move as slide 1, one timeframe lower.
Step 2 · Mark the zone
30m: the demand at the origin of the shift
What is marked
The sweep. The line at the lower left is the old low. The wick goes through it.
X. After the first bounce, a small low is taken once more.
30m Demand and IMB. A large bullish candle follows that second sweep. The demand is drawn at its base and the imbalance sits above it.
$$ on a dotted rising line. Lows climbing in a row above the zone. This is trendline liquidity.
MSS, then BoS. Price closes above the high before the drop, pulls back, and breaks to a higher high.
Why this is the zone
It is the base of the candle that started the shift, and it formed right after a sweep. Everything above it formed later: the rising lows with $$ and the pullback low before the BoS. Those are liquidity, and they sit between price and the zone.
Rule to carry forward
Draw the 30m demand at the base of the displacement that led to the shift. Then mark every low that forms above it. Expect those lows to be taken before the zone is reached.

entries.h: 30m: inducement taken, zone tapped
entries.t:
Chart: 30-minute USD/JPY chart, later. After the break of structure price rallies to a peak, then declines. It falls through the pullback low marked IDM, one large candle reaches the top of the 30-minute demand zone, and price bounces and breaks a lower high (MSS).
Slide 3 — “30m Timeframes.” Later in time.
Step 3 · Wait for the return
30m: inducement taken, zone tapped
What happened
The rally continued, then topped. After the BoS price ran to a peak and rolled over.
The decline was steady. Lower highs and lower lows all the way down.
The IDM low was taken. That is the pullback low from before the BoS. Anyone who bought there, or trailed a stop under it, was taken out.
The 30m demand was tapped. One large bearish candle reached into the top part of the zone and price turned up at once.
MSS. The bounce closed above the last lower high of the decline.
Why this matters
Buying the pullback low before the BoS was the obvious trade and it failed. The inducement page describes this exactly: the first clean low after a shift is bait, and the real zone is the one underneath it.
The peak of this rally is now the high the decline started from. It becomes the target on slide 5.
Rule to carry forward
Wait for price to take the inducement low and reach the 30m demand. Then change to the 15m and ask for a sweep and a shift there.

entries.h: 15m: sweep and shift at the 30m demand
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute USD/JPY chart. Price falls into the 30-minute demand zone and bounces. A small low is swept (X). A displacement candle leaves an imbalance and a 15-minute demand zone, and price closes above the prior high (MSS). A pullback low afterwards is marked IDM.
Slide 4 — “15mTimeframes.” The lower-left box is the 30m demand.
Step 4 · Sweep, shift, zone
15m: sweep and shift at the 30m demand
What happened
The tap. A wick reaches into the 30m demand and price bounces hard.
A 15m sweep (X). The bounce pauses and leaves a small low. A wick runs under it and closes back up. This low is above the low of the tap.
Displacement and IMB. A run of bullish candles leaves an imbalance.
MSS. Price closes above the high from before the final drop.
15m demand. Drawn at the base of the displacement, under the imbalance.
IDM. Price goes sideways and leaves a pullback low above the zone.
Why this matters
This is the 1H sequence again in miniature: sweep, shift, zone. The 30m demand gave the location. The 15m gives the proof and a much smaller zone to trade from.
The new IDM low is the next piece of bait. It sits between price and the 15m demand, so expect it to be taken before the fill.
Rule to carry forward
At the HTF zone, wait for a 15m low to be swept and a 15m close above the last high. Draw the demand at the base of that move. Label the first pullback low after it as inducement, not as an entry.

entries.h: 15m: entry, stop and target on one chart
entries.t:
Chart: Wider 15-minute USD/JPY chart with the long planned. A BSL line runs from the far-left high. Price has declined through the IDM level into the 30-minute demand, swept a low (X), shifted (MSS) and left a 15-minute demand. The position box has its entry at the top of the 15-minute demand, its stop at the X sweep low and its target at the BSL line.
Slide 5 — “15mTimeframes.” The plan.
Step 5 · Plan the trade
15m: entry, stop and target on one chart
What is marked
BSL. A line from the high at the far left, where the whole decline began. This is the peak from slide 3.
IDM (left). The 30m inducement level that price fell through.
30m Demand, X, MSS, IMB, 15m demand, IDM. Everything from slide 4.
The position box. Entry at the top edge of the 15m demand. Stop at the X sweep low, where the line from the X meets the bottom of the grey box. Target at the BSL line.
Reading the box
The target is about 3.3 times the stop. Price has not come back yet. This is a resting limit order with all three prices fixed in advance.
The stop is under the 15m sweep low. It is not under the low of the tap into the 30m demand, which is lower. That keeps the stop small. It also means a second, deeper test of the 30m demand would stop the trade out.
Rule to carry forward
Target the high the pullback into the HTF zone started from. If the distance from the 15m demand to that high is less than twice the stop, there is no trade.

entries.h: Result: a deep fill, then the target
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute USD/JPY result. After the IDM low forms, price spikes to a new high, then falls through the IDM low deep into the 15-minute demand without reaching the stop. It bounces, makes a higher low, rallies, pauses, and one large candle carries it through the BSL line toward a higher unlabelled line.
Slide 6 — “Result.”
Step 6 · Result
Result: a deep fill, then the target
What happened
One more push up. Before coming back, price spiked above the highs of the range. The slide does not label it. I read it as buy-side being taken before the pullback.
The IDM low was taken. Price fell straight through it.
A deep fill. Price went through most of the 15m demand. The wick stopped near the bottom of the zone, above the stop.
A higher low. The first bounce was sold once more. That dip held above the zone.
The rally. Price climbed, paused about halfway, and then one large candle went through the BSL line.
Beyond the target. Price kept rising toward an unlabelled line higher up.
What to take from it
The order at the top edge filled, and the trade then went against the entry by most of the zone's height. That is normal for an edge entry.
The stop held because it was under the sweep low, not inside the zone.
The pause halfway is where a trader who moved the stop up too early, or closed out of boredom, lost the trade.

entries.h: The whole trade on one page
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole trade on one page
Chart: Cover slide: USDJPY Case Study Breakdown, showing the finished 15-minute trade.
Cover — “USDJPY Case Study Breakdown.”
The same three-step pattern runs twice. First on the 1H and 30m to give the bias and the zone. Then on the 15m, at that zone, to give the entry.
| Stage | First pass (1H / 30m) | Second pass (15m)
| Sweep | The old low, then a minor low (X) | A minor low after the tap of the 30m demand (X)
| Shift | 1H and 30m close above the high before the drop | 15m close above the high before the final drop
| Zone | 30m demand at the base of the displacement | 15m demand at the base of the displacement
| Inducement | Rising lows ($$) and the pullback low before the BoS | The pullback low after the 15m shift
| Return | IDM taken, 30m demand tapped | IDM taken, 15m demand filled deep
1 · BIAS
The 1H sweeps an old low and closes above the high before the drop. Long bias.
2 · LOCATION
The 30m demand at the base of that move. Price rallies, tops, and comes back through the inducement low to tap it.
3 · CONFIRMATION
On the 15m, a low is swept at the zone and price shifts up with an imbalance, leaving the 15m demand.
4 · ENTRY
Price takes the 15m inducement low and fills the buy limit at the top of the 15m demand. The fill goes deep and holds.
5 · TARGET
Price returns to the high the pullback began from and goes through it. About 3.3R.
THE LOGIC IN ONE SENTENCE
After a 1H sweep and shift, wait for price to come back to the 30m demand, let the 15m sweep and shift there, and buy the 15m demand toward the high above.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Buy limit at the top edge of the 15m demand.
The zone is the base of the 15m displacement, under the imbalance.
Price went through most of the zone after the fill. Expect drawdown on an edge entry.
A lower entry inside the zone would also have filled here, with a smaller stop. It would have missed the trades where price only touches the edge.
Stop loss
Below the 15m sweep low (X), plus a buffer.
The grey box ends at the X low. That low sits under the 15m demand and above the 30m demand.
If it breaks, the 15m sweep is undone and the shift is void.
The safer alternative is under the low of the tap into the 30m demand. It is wider and cuts the reward-to-risk.
Leave a few pips below the wick. Sell stops trigger on the bid, so no spread needs adding on a long.
Take profit
The BSL line: the high before the drop. About 3.3R.
It is the high the decline into the 30m demand started from.
No opposing supply zone is marked. The target is liquidity.
Price went well past it. The plan still exits at the line. Set the order a few pips before it.

Position size
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the lot size.
Lots = money at risk ÷ (stop in pips × pip value per lot)
On USD/JPY one standard lot moves ¥1,000 per pip. In dollars that is 1,000 ÷ the USD/JPY rate, for example about $6.67 at 150.00.
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. Stop of 15 pips at $6.67 per pip per lot gives 100 ÷ (15 × 6.67) ≈ 1.0 lot. At 1:3.3 the target pays about $330. The 15 pips is an illustration. The slides show no prices.
