entries.h: HTF zone tapped
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour USD/JPY chart. Price sweeps a low, breaks structure upward (MSS), rallies, then pulls back into the 4H demand zone and reacts.
Slide 1 — 4H chart. Tap to enlarge.
Step 1 · Location and bias
HTF zone tapped
This slide answers the first question of any trade: which direction, and from where?
What happened
Sell-side liquidity was swept. At the bottom left, a horizontal line marks an earlier low. A long wick drives below it and price closes back above. Stops under that low were taken and nobody followed through to the downside.
Structure shifted bullish (MSS). Price then closed above the swing high that had produced the low. On the 4H that turns the bias from bearish to bullish.
A demand zone was left behind. The 4H demand box is drawn around the last consolidation before the candle that broke structure. That is where the buying that changed the trend originated.
Price rallied, then came back. After several days of higher highs, price retraced the whole way down and wicked into the zone for the first time. The final candle on the slide is a strong bullish reaction out of it.
Why this zone is worth trading
It did something. It caused the MSS. Zones that break structure carry more weight than zones that merely paused price.
It is fresh. This is the first return. A zone that has already been tapped has had its orders used.
It is in discount. The zone sits in the lower half of the leg from the swept low to the high. Longs are bought cheap, not chased.
It was born from a sweep. Liquidity grab, then shift, then zone. That order of events is what gives the zone its quality.
Rule to carry forward
Only look for longs when price is inside a fresh HTF demand zone that caused a break of structure and sits in discount. Until price gets there, there is nothing to do. The 4H tap is a reason to watch, not a reason to buy.

entries.h: 30m market shift
entries.t:
Chart: 30-minute USD/JPY chart. Price sells off from a 30m supply zone, breaks a low into the 4H demand zone, then breaks the last lower high (MSS).
Slide 2 — 30m chart. The large olive box is the 4H demand from slide 1.
Step 2 · Confirmation
30m market shift
Dropping to the 30m shows how price arrived at the 4H zone and whether buyers actually showed up. This slide is the “confirmation” in the title.
What happened
The delivery was bearish. From the 30m supply at the top, price made a clean sequence of lower highs and lower lows. Inside the HTF pullback, the 30m trend was down.
30m supply is marked at the origin. It is the base of the sell-off. A dotted line runs from a later high that already wicked up toward it, so buy-side liquidity is resting right at the lower edge of that zone. This becomes the target.
The last low was broken into demand (BoS). The dashed BoS line marks the final 30m low. Price pushes under it and lands inside the 4H demand. On the 30m this looks like bearish continuation. In context, it is a run on sell-side liquidity into a HTF buy zone.
The break failed to continue. There was no follow-through below the BoS. Price reversed from inside the zone.
MSS. A strong bullish leg closed above the last lower high, the high that had produced the final low. The 30m sequence of lower highs is over.
Why this matters
A HTF zone can fail. Buying the first touch means paying for a wide stop below the whole 4H zone and accepting that price may slice straight through. Waiting for the 30m shift costs a few pips of entry price and buys proof that the 4H demand is being defended. It also produces a much tighter stop, which is where the 1:3 comes from.
Rule to carry forward
Inside the HTF zone, wait for three things in this order: a low is taken, price fails to continue lower, and a candle closes above the last lower high with displacement. A wick through the high does not count.
Common mistake
Calling an MSS on a break of a minor internal high. The high that matters is the one that led to the lowest low. On this slide the MSS line starts from that swing, not from the small bounces underneath it.

entries.h: 15m entry
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute USD/JPY chart at the moment of the shift. A 15m order block sits under an imbalance; a long position is planned from the order block to the 30m supply.
Slide 3 — 15m chart at the moment the order is planned. Grey box is risk, blue box is reward.
Step 3 · Refinement and order placement
15m entry
The 30m gave permission. The 15m gives the price. This slide is frozen just after the shift, before the pullback, which is when the limit order is placed.
What is marked
$$$ on the descending line. Each lower high on the way down sits on a trendline. Breakout traders and trailing stops cluster above lines like this, so it is buy-side liquidity and part of what draws price upward.
BoS into 4H demand. The same sweep as slide 2, seen in more detail.
X = liquidity sweep. After the first bounce out of the 4H demand, price dipped once more and a wick ran the small lows left by that bounce, then closed back up. X marks that sweep. It cleared the last sell-side liquidity sitting under price, and the displacement candle followed straight after. The solid line drawn from the sweep's low runs to the bottom of the grey risk box, so that low is also the trade's invalidation.
MSS. One large bullish candle closes through the lower high. That is displacement: speed and range, not a slow grind.
IMB (imbalance). The displacement candle moved so fast that it left a gap in price delivery just above the order block. Price tends to return to rebalance these gaps, which is why a pullback is expected at all.
15m OB. The last bearish candle area before the displacement. It sits directly under the imbalance, so a pullback that fills the IMB arrives at the OB.
Why the entry is here and not elsewhere
The order block is the origin of the move that broke structure. It is inside the 4H demand, below the midpoint of the new bullish leg, and it has an imbalance above it to pull price back. Entry is a buy limit at the top edge of the OB, which is the first price the pullback reaches after filling the imbalance.
The opposing 30m supply is far enough away to pay about three times the risk. If supply had been sitting just above the MSS high, the same pattern would not have been worth taking.
Rule to carry forward
After the MSS, mark the last opposing candle before the displacement. Take it only if it has an imbalance next to it and has not been touched since. Place the limit order immediately; do not chase the breakout candle.

entries.h: Result
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute USD/JPY chart after the trade. Price pulls back into the order block, then rallies through the blue reward box to the 30m supply zone.
Slide 4 — the same 15m chart after the trade played out.
Step 4 · Management and outcome
Result
What happened
Price paused at the MSS high. A few small candles drifted sideways and down. No new low was made.
The imbalance was filled. Price traded back through the IMB.
The OB was tapped by a wick. One candle dipped into the top of the 15m order block and closed back above it. The limit order filled there. Price never came close to the X sweep low.
Expansion. Price rallied in two legs with a shallow pullback between them, taking the highs along the trendline on the way.
Target reached. The top of the blue box is the lower edge of the 30m supply. Price hit it and pushed slightly into the zone.
What to take from it
The fill was shallow. Only a wick entered the OB. An order at the middle or bottom of the OB may not have filled. Entering at the top edge costs a little reward-to-risk and gets you into more trades.
The pullback took time. There were roughly two to three hours on the chart between the shift and the fill. The setup rewards patience with a resting order, not screen-watching.
The target was the zone edge. Taking profit at the first touch of supply meant the trade was closed before any reaction from sellers. What price did afterwards is not shown and is not the trade's concern.
Rule to carry forward
Once filled, do nothing until price either reaches the target or makes a new structural high. Moving the stop early on a 15m wobble is the usual way a 1:3 winner turns into a breakeven.

entries.h: The whole trade in a single picture
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole trade in a single picture
A schematic of the sequence, not a copy of the chart. Read it left to right.
1 · SWEEP INTO THE ZONE
The 30m downtrend breaks its last low and lands in the fresh 4H demand. Sell stops are taken where higher-timeframe buyers are waiting.
2 · SHIFT
A final liquidity sweep (X) clears the lows under price, and a displacement candle closes above the last lower high. The 30m has turned to agree with the 4H.
3 · ENTRY
The displacement leaves an imbalance above a 15m order block. Price returns, fills the imbalance and taps the top of the OB, where the buy limit is resting.
4 · TARGET
Price expands through the trendline highs to the lower edge of the 30m supply that started the sell-off. The trade closes there at about 3R.
The logic in one sentence
Buy the first pullback after lower-timeframe structure flips inside a higher-timeframe demand zone, risk the low that made the flip, and take profit at the nearest opposing zone.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Buy limit at the top edge of the 15m order block.
Place it as soon as the MSS candle closes.
The top edge is where the imbalance ends, so it is the first price a pullback reaches.
In this trade only a wick reached the OB. A deeper order risked no fill.
Add the spread to a buy limit. Buys fill on the ask, which is above the charted price.
Stop loss
Below the low of the X liquidity sweep, plus a small buffer.
The X sweep is the low that launched the MSS. The liquidity there has already been taken, so price has no reason to return. If it does break, the bullish shift is void and the reason for the trade is gone.
This is lower than the bottom of the OB. A stop tucked just under the OB is exposed to a slightly deeper wick.
Buffer: a few pips below the wick. Sell stops trigger on the bid, so the spread does not need to be added on a long.
More conservative: below the sweep low inside the 4H zone. Safer, and it lowers the reward-to-risk.
Take profit
Lower edge of the 30m supply. About 3R.
It is the first opposing zone, and the origin of the sell-off. Sellers may be waiting there.
The trendline highs ($$$) and the earlier high near the zone edge are liquidity that pulls price up to it.
The target is the near edge, not inside the zone. Do not ask price to push through sellers to pay you.
Set the order a touch below the edge. Price often turns a few pips short of a zone.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
Leave the stop alone until price closes above the MSS high and prints a new 15m higher low. Then it can trail to just under that higher low.
Optional partial at the MSS high or at the trendline liquidity if you want to pay yourself early. Decide this before entry, not during.
Cancel the limit if price reaches about half of the way to target without filling you. The reward that justified the trade is no longer there.
Position size
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the lot size.
Lots = money at risk ÷ (stop in pips × pip value per lot)
On USD/JPY one standard lot moves ¥1,000 per pip. In dollars that is 1,000 ÷ the USD/JPY rate, for example about $6.67 at 150.00.
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. Stop of 15 pips at $6.67 per pip per lot gives 100 ÷ (15 × 6.67) ≈ 1.0 lot. At 1:3 the target pays about $300.

entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Work down the list in order. Each step is a yes or no. A “no” ends the process for that pair. For shorts, mirror everything: supply for demand, highs for lows.
Mark the 4H structure and its zones.Find the last break of structure. Mark the demand zone that caused it. Check it is untouched and in the lower half of the leg.
Wait for price to enter the zone.Set an alert at the top edge. No alert, no analysis.
Drop to the 30m and map the way in.Mark the lower highs and lower lows of the pullback, the last low, and the supply zone at its origin. That supply is your likely target.
Did price take a low inside the zone?You want the last 30m low run while price is in HTF demand. No sweep means the liquidity is still below you.
Did a candle close above the last lower high with displacement?This is the MSS. It must be a close, from a large-bodied candle, through the high that produced the lowest low.
On the 15m, is there an order block with an imbalance beside it?Mark the last bearish candle before the displacement. It should be unmitigated and sit inside the HTF zone.
Does the trade pay at least 1:2 to the first opposing zone?Measure entry at the OB top, stop under the sweep low that launched the MSS, target at the near edge of supply. Under 1:2, skip it.
Place the orders.Buy limit, stop loss and take profit together. Size the position for a fixed risk of 0.5–1% of the account.
Manage by structure, then record it.Hold until target, stop, or a new structural high lets you trail. Screenshot the 4H, 30m and 15m and log the result, win or lose.

entries.h: When this setup should be skipped
entries.t:
Filters
When this setup should be skipped
Do not take it if
The 4H zone has already been tapped and reacted once.
Price closes a 4H candle below the bottom of the demand zone.
The “shift” is a wick through the high, or a slow overlapping crawl with no imbalance.
The opposing supply is so close that the trade pays less than 1:2.
Price runs to target without pulling back. The trade is missed, not chased.
High-impact news for USD or JPY is due before the pullback is likely to fill.
This trade had all of these
Fresh 4H demand that caused a 4H MSS, in discount.
Sell-side liquidity taken on the way into the zone.
30m MSS on a single displacement candle.
Imbalance sitting directly on a 15m order block.
A second liquidity sweep (X) just before the shift, giving a clear low for the stop.
Unmitigated 30m supply about 3R away, with trendline liquidity along the path.
Keep this in proportion
This is one trade, chosen for a post because it worked. The same pattern also loses: the zone fails, the order block is run, or price never pulls back. What makes it a strategy is taking every valid occurrence with the same risk and counting the results. Collect at least 50 examples in backtesting, losers included, before trusting the numbers.

entries.h: 4H: sweep the high, shift down
entries.t:
Chart: 4-hour gold chart. A wick takes out an earlier high (X), price sells off and closes below the previous swing low (MSS), then bounces.
Slide 1 — 4H chart. “Price sweeps the high, then shifts structure down.”
Step 1 · Bias
4H: sweep the high, shift down
This slide sets the direction for everything that follows.
What happened
An old high was left standing. The first peak on the left is the reference high. Buy stops from sellers and breakout orders from buyers collect above it.
Price came back and swept it (X). Days later a candle pushed above that high and could not hold there. The following candles closed back underneath. The buy-side liquidity was taken and there was no continuation.
Structure shifted bearish (MSS). The sell-off that followed closed below the swing low between the two peaks. The 4H is no longer making higher lows.
A pullback began. The last few candles on the slide are a bounce off the low. That bounce is what the lower timeframes zoom into.
Why this matters
Sweep, then shift. A break of structure that comes straight after a liquidity grab is more trustworthy than one that comes from nowhere. The high was used to fill sell orders.
The bounce is now a selling opportunity. After a bearish 4H MSS, rallies are pullbacks until proven otherwise. The job is to find where the pullback ends.
The trade is with the higher timeframe. Everything below is about timing a short in the direction the 4H has already chosen.
Rule to carry forward
Take shorts only after the 4H has swept a high and closed below the last swing low. Then wait for the pullback. Do not sell the breakdown candle itself: it is the most expensive place to enter.

entries.h: 1H: the pullback runs an internal high
entries.t:
Chart: 1-hour gold chart. After a steep drop, price climbs back, takes out an internal high from inside the drop (X), takes one more small high (X), then prints a bearish candle.
Slide 2 — 1H chart. “Zoom in. Price pullback, sweep internal high and start moving down.”
Step 2 · Location and liquidity
1H: the pullback runs an internal high
The 1H shows how far the bounce travels and what it takes on the way.
What happened
The drop left an internal high. Partway down the sell-off, one candle made a small high before price continued lower. The long X line starts from it. Traders who sold the drop tend to put stops above a high like this.
Price climbed back in a slow grind. Small overlapping candles for many hours. Compare that with the speed of the drop: the pullback is corrective, the drop was impulsive.
First sweep (long X). A large bullish candle finally pushed through the internal high. By then price had recovered well over half of the drop, so it was in premium.
Second sweep (short X). Price made one more marginal high above the candle that did the first sweep, with wicks only.
A bearish candle followed. The last candle on the slide is the first decisive move down since the pullback began.
Why this is the location
There is no supply box drawn on this slide. The point of interest is the liquidity itself. The pullback has reached the upper half of the bearish leg and has taken the stops that were resting inside it. Sellers now have both a good price and the orders they need to fill against.
Rule to carry forward
In a bearish pullback, mark the internal highs left inside the drop. The short setup begins when price is above the 50% level of the leg and one of those highs has been swept. Before that, the pullback is still shopping for liquidity.
Common mistake
Selling the first touch of the internal high. Price swept it and then went on to take a second high on the 1H and a third on the 15m. The sweep says “watch”. Only a structure shift says “sell”.

entries.h: 15m: three breaks up, a sweep, then the shift
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute gold chart. Three breaks of structure upward, a sweep of the higher-timeframe high (X), a second sweep (X), then a close below the last higher low (MSS).
Slide 3 — 15m chart. “Structure breaks up a few times. Then price sweeps the high and shifts down.”
Step 3 · Confirmation
15m: three breaks up, a sweep, then the shift
What happened
The 15m was bullish on the way up. Three BoS labels mark three higher highs. On this timeframe alone, it looks like an uptrend worth buying.
The 1H internal high was taken (long X). The long horizontal line is the same high from slide 2. The third leg up runs straight through it.
A higher low formed, then one more high (short X). Price dipped, then pushed up again and took the high it had just made. This is the second sweep.
MSS. Price then closed below the higher low that sat between the two sweeps. For the first time in the whole rally, a 15m low failed.
Why this matters
Each break of structure on the way up recruits buyers and gives them a place to put stops. By the third one, the lows underneath are loaded with sell stops and late buyers are entering at the highs, exactly where the 4H wants to sell. The MSS is the first evidence that the 15m has stopped disagreeing with the 4H.
Rule to carry forward
Let the lower timeframe trend against you into the higher-timeframe liquidity. The signal is the sequence: the HTF high is swept, then a candle closes below the most recent 15m higher low. Use the low that produced the final high, not a minor one inside the last leg.

entries.h: Entry: order block under a protected high
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute gold chart with the short planned. An order block sits above an imbalance and below the protected high; the target is the top of the demand zone, with equal lows on the way.
Slide 4 — 15m chart with the order planned. “Price returns to the order block and the protected high stays intact.”
Step 4 · Refinement and order placement
Entry: order block under a protected high
This slide is frozen shortly after the shift. Everything needed to place the order is on it.
What is marked
A third X and the protected high. Just before the drop, one wick took out a small high. That wick is the last high made before the displacement, so it becomes the protected high. If price trades above it, the bearish shift has failed.
OB. The last bullish candles before the displacement candle. This is where the selling that broke structure began.
IMB. The displacement candle left an imbalance directly under the order block. A pullback that fills it arrives at the bottom of the OB.
MSS. The broken higher low, a little below the OB.
EQL. Equal lows left during the rally. Two lows at the same price mean a thick layer of sell stops underneath. It sits between entry and target and helps pull price down.
Demand. The zone at the base of the 15m rally. It is the first place buyers are likely to respond, so the target is its top edge.
Why the entry is here
The order block is the origin of the move that broke structure, it sits in premium on every timeframe shown, and the imbalance beneath it gives price a reason to come back. Entry is a sell limit at the bottom edge of the OB, the first price a pullback reaches after filling the imbalance.
The stop on the chart sits just above the top of the order block, a little under the protected high. That keeps the risk small. Measured against it, the distance down to demand is about 3.8 times the risk.
Rule to carry forward
After a bearish MSS, mark the last bullish candle before the displacement and the high above it. Sell the bottom edge of that order block only while the protected high is intact and only if an imbalance separates the OB from current price.

entries.h: Result
entries.t:
Chart: 15-minute gold chart after the trade. Price ranges below the order block, spikes into its bottom edge, then sells off through the equal lows to the top of the demand zone.
Slide 5 — the same chart after the trade played out.
Step 5 · Management and outcome
Result
What happened
Price went sideways first. For roughly two hours after the shift it ranged underneath the order block without reaching it.
One push filled the order. Around 06:00 on the chart a candle ran up through the imbalance and touched the bottom of the OB. The next candle was strongly bearish.
The protected high was never tested. Price did not travel past the lower part of the order block.
Sell-off through the equal lows. Price fell in a steady staircase, cleared the EQL, and kept going.
Target reached. The bottom of the blue box is the top edge of demand. Price hit it and wicked slightly inside.
What to take from it
The fill was shallow again. As in the USD/JPY trade, price only just reached the near edge of the order block. A sell limit in the middle of the OB would have been left behind.
The range before the fill was a test of patience. Nothing in those two hours changed the plan: the protected high was intact and the order was resting.
Equal lows were fuel, not the exit. The target was the demand zone beyond them. The EQL is a sensible place for a partial if you take one.
Rule to carry forward
While waiting for a fill, the only question is whether the protected high has been broken. If it has, cancel. If it has not, leave the order alone.

entries.h: The whole trade in a single picture
entries.t:
Everything as one
The whole trade in a single picture
A schematic of the 15m sequence, not a copy of the chart. The 4H has already swept its high and shifted bearish before this picture starts.
1 · SWEEP THE HTF HIGH
The 15m rallies out of demand with three breaks of structure and runs the 1H internal high. Stops above the pullback are taken in premium.
2 · SWEEP AGAIN
A higher low forms, then price takes the high it just made. A last small sweep sets the protected high.
3 · SHIFT
A displacement candle closes below the higher low. It leaves an imbalance under the order block.
4 · ENTRY
After a two-hour range, price fills the imbalance and touches the bottom of the order block, where the sell limit is resting.
5 · TARGET
Price sells off through the equal lows to the top of the demand zone that started the rally. About 3.8R.
THE LOGIC IN ONE SENTENCE
Sell the first pullback after the 15m flips bearish at swept HTF highs, risk the order block, and take profit at the first demand below.

entries.h: Entry, stop loss and take profit
entries.t:
Order placement
Entry, stop loss and take profit
Entry
Sell limit at the bottom edge of the 15m order block.
Place it when the MSS candle closes.
The bottom edge is where the imbalance ends, so it is the first price a pullback reaches.
Price only touched that edge here. A deeper order would not have filled.
Sells fill on the bid, which is the charted price. No spread adjustment is needed on the entry.
Stop loss
Just above the top of the order block, plus spread.
This is where the grey box ends on the chart: above the OB, slightly below the protected high.
Reason: if price trades through the whole order block, the sellers there have been absorbed.
A short is closed by a buy stop, which triggers on the ask. Gold spreads can be wide, so add the spread to the stop.
More conservative: above the protected high. That is the true structural invalidation. On this chart it would have cut the trade to roughly 1:3.
Take profit
Top edge of the demand zone. About 3.8R.
It is the first opposing zone: the base of the rally that carried price up into the highs.
The equal lows sit above it, so price has liquidity to reach for on the way down.
The target is the near edge. Buyers may respond anywhere inside the zone.
A short's take profit fills on the ask. Set it a little above the zone edge, by the spread plus a small margin.
Managing the position
The post shows a single entry and a single exit. The points below are my suggested handling, not something marked on the slides.
Leave the stop alone until price closes below the post-MSS low and prints a new 15m lower high. Then it can trail to just above that lower high.
Optional partial at the equal lows. Decide before entry.
Cancel the limit if the protected high breaks, or if price covers about half the distance to demand without filling you.
Position size on gold
Fix the money at risk first, then let the stop distance decide the lot size.
Lots = money at risk ÷ (stop in dollars × 100)
One standard lot of XAU/USD is normally 100 ounces, so a $1 move in gold is $100 per lot. Check your broker's contract size, because some differ.
Example: $10,000 account, 1% risk = $100. A stop of $5.00 gives 100 ÷ (5 × 100) = 0.20 lots. At 1:3.8 the target pays about $380.

entries.h: Step-by-step for the next trade
entries.t:
Repeatable strategy
Step-by-step for the next trade
Written for shorts, as in this trade. For longs, mirror it: lows for highs, discount for premium, supply for demand. A “no” at any step ends the process.
Has the 4H swept a high and closed below the last swing low?Both are needed. This gives the bearish bias. Mark the leg from the swept high to the new low and its 50% level.
On the 1H, mark the internal highs inside the drop.These are the liquidity the pullback is likely to reach for. Set an alert at the nearest one above the 50% level.
Has the pullback swept an internal high in premium?It should arrive as a corrective grind, slower than the drop. No sweep, no setup.
Drop to the 15m and mark the most recent higher low.The rally will show several breaks of structure up. Keep moving the line to the low that produced the latest high.
Did a candle close below that higher low with displacement?This is the MSS. It should leave an imbalance. A wick below the low does not count.
Mark the order block and the protected high.The OB is the last bullish candle before the displacement. The protected high is the highest point just before the drop. The OB must be untouched since the shift.
Does it pay at least 1:2 to the first demand below?Measure entry at the OB's bottom edge, stop above the OB (or above the protected high), target at the top edge of demand.
Place the orders.Sell limit, stop and target together. Size for a fixed 0.5–1% of the account. Add the spread to the stop.
Manage by structure, then record it.Cancel if the protected high breaks before the fill. Once in, hold to target, stop, or a new lower high you can trail above. Screenshot the 4H, 1H and 15m.
